title: KBO’s LG Twins Extend Austin Dean
content:
The LG Twins of the KBO announced a contract extension for first baseman Austin Dean this week. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $2MM.

Dean has been one of the top hitters in Korea since making the move in 2023. He’s hit .320 with 127 homers in four seasons with the Twins. He has 11 more long balls than the next-closest player in that span, which happens to be Si Hwan Roh, who was recently posted for MLB teams by the Hanwha Eagles.

The 33-year-old Dean was drafted by the Marlins in the fourth round of the 2012 draft. He hit well in the minors, but didn’t debut with Miami until 2018. Dean posted a .656 OPS in parts of two seasons as a Marlin. He was dealt to the Cardinals in a minor trade before the 2020 campaign.

After playing sparingly in the shortened season, Dean broke camp with the Cardinals in 2021. He saw minimal work off the bench and was sent down a month into the year. Dean was bumped off the roster at the end of the season and claimed by the Giants. He spent the majority of his time in San Francisco’s organization at Triple-A.

Dean was a subpar outfielder in the majors, recording -15 Defensive Runs Saved in 96 games. He’s played almost exclusively first base and DH with the Twins. The power-hitting righty with limited defensive viability tends to be a tough roster fit in the majors. It might be difficult for Dean to find a gig if he tried to make a return to the majors. He seems content to keep mashing in Korea.

Young Casario, a three-star recruit from Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School, a private boarding school in North Georgia, was just 18 years.

He had committed to play for the Bulldogs just five months before his death.

Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School confirmed that a “medical incident” occurred, but an official cause of death has not been revealed at this time. After his death was announced, tributes began to pour out on social media.

title: Pat McAfee showed up to ‘College GameDay’ on a horse
content:
ESPN’s traveling road show College GameDay was in Boise, Idaho on Saturday for the first time in 16 years ahead of No. 24 Boise State’s showdown with Oregon State. With a win, the Broncos can secure their spot in the Pac-12 title game and continue their march towards a potential spot in the College Football Playoff.

It was a packed house for GameDay, with Boise State fans showing up in droves despite the early call-time — it was still dark out when the show first went on the air. Notably, Pat McAfee was absent from the GameDay desk at the very start of the show, but only because he was waiting to make a grand entrance.

“As you might have heard, people have had some travel difficulties,” host Rece Davis teased, referencing the nationwide flight delays that made travel impossible for much of Friday. “That includes Pat McAfee. Pat is trying to find his way here. We’re certainly hopeful that we find him soon, and that McAfee can make it to the set.”

At that point, McAfee called out, “Rece! Rece Davis can you hear me?” Cameras cut to McAfee riding on horseback alongside Boise State handlers and representatives carrying a school flag.

“Don’t you worry about an airplane. Don’t you worry about an automobile. I’m riding on Rodeo. A horse, that was of course, built to be amongst these Broncos fans,” McAfee said, throwing in some “Whoaaaaaaas” when necessary as his horse got a little excited.

“Thank you Kathy Joe, you’re the best,” McAfee said as he dismounted. He then thanked the rest of the crew that helped him in and began running towards the desk.

“This particular Saturday is going to be a magical one,” McAfee said. “There’s going to be chaos, implications across the country as people will be punching their ticket to the College Football Playoff.”

Once at the desk, McAfee exhaled a bit.

“That horse’s name was Rodeo, and I will say to Rodeo, thank you for not bucking my ass off. A magical morning here at Boise State. I’ve never ridden a horse before. I certainly lied to them to let that happen.”

Rece Davis: “And as you might have heard, people have had some travel difficulties… That includes Pat McAfee…”

Pat McAfee arrives on horseback to open ‘College GameDay’ in Boise.

McAfee: “I have never rode a horse before. I certainly lied to them to let that happen.” https://t.co/Wopf4svRuo

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 14, 2026

McAfee’s presence on GameDay has come under more scrutiny this year, but this felt like a return to the type of bits that found him success early on in his run with the show.

While there’s always going to be a segment of fans that have simply had enough of McAfee due to his overexposure, his best moments on GameDay are ones like this that come from embracing the school he’s at, rather than pushing up against it.

Henderson said the condition impacted his physical ability in a season where he's ran for 203 yards and one touchdown over six games. title: Why Is Mauricio Pochettino Still USA's Manager As Manchester United's New Hire?
content: If someone had said that one of the big names on the U.S. men's national team would be joining Manchester United in the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup, you would have thought a player. Instead, it will be Mauricio Pochettino. The 54-year-old Argentine was named Manchester United's new manager on Nov. 13, after having signed a contract extension with U.S. Soccer in August that would have run through the 2030 World Cup. But before he leaves for Old Trafford, Pochettino will lead the Americans for two final games, on Saturday and Tuesday vs. Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals. Pochettino's first game with the beleaguered Premier League powerhouse will be the Nov. 22 trip to rivals Liverpool. So how is Pochettino technically in charge of both the USMNT and Manchester United at the same time? It's more of a matter of timing. Man United is on break for the international window, when players return to their national teams for official FIFA matches, so Pochettino can finish out the Haiti series. An immediate departure would have left the U.S. in the lurch, especially since Manchester United also hired his coaching staff. "It all was so quick," an emotional Pochettino said Friday after he confirmed his exit. As part of the agreement with Manchester United, the club paid U.S. Soccer a reported $10 million to release Pochettino from his contract – along with an additional $2 million for the staff. "Those funds are used to help us hire great coaches," U.S. Soccer CEO JT Batson said Friday. "Our supporters, our sponsors, our donors, our fans are very supportive around making sure that we have the resources to achieve our goals, including having a world-class coach." Two Jobs At Once: Does It Happen Often? It's very rare for a coach to be in charge of two teams at once. When it happens, it's usually a club coach stepping in as an interim manager for a national team. If you go way back in time, Alex Ferguson (before adding "Sir" to his name due to becoming a Manchester United legend) managed Aberdeen while also leading Scotland's national team at the 1986 World Cup. In 2009, Guus Hiddink was Russia’s manager while also serving as Chelsea’s interim boss. Ricardo "Tuca" Ferretti was Mexico's caretaker on three occasions (1993, 2015, 2018) throughout his storied Liga MX managerial career. Perhaps the most infamous recent case of a coach being tied to both club and country occurred when Real Madrid announced Spain manager Julen Lopetegui as its next coach two days before the 2018 World Cup. The plan was for him to take over once the World Cup concluded. Instead, the Spanish soccer federation fired him on the eve of the tournament. Spain was knocked out in the round of 16 under interim Fernando Hierro, and Lopetegui lasted only a few months at Real Madrid.

title: A’s Receiving Trade Interest In Jacob Wilson
content:
Jacob Wilson’s All-Star rookie season was followed up by an injury-plagued 2026 campaign, as the Athletics’ shortstop hit only .266/.298/.388 over 337 plate appearances.  Wilson sprained his left shoulder in May while diving for a Gunnar Henderson grounder, and while he missed only a month on the injured list, renewed shoulder discomfort sent him back to the IL for good in late August, and Wilson underwent a season-ending surgery on his troublesome shoulder in early September.

Despite this rough sophomore year and the $66MM remaining on Wilson’s contract, the shortstop has been drawing trade interest, according to USA Today’s Bob Nightengale.  This could just be some due diligence from rival clubs, or explorations to see if the A’s would bite on a lowball offer.  There isn’t any indication that the A’s are even considering moving Wilson, and a trade would be pretty surprising given that Wilson signed his long-term extension with the club just last January.

It should be noted that Wilson’s extension was signed under former GM David Forst, so new president of baseball operations Taylor Smith could have a different view of Wilson as a long-term cornerstone.  There haven’t been any updates on Wilson’s recovery timeline, so if he will miss a decent chunk of the 2027 season, that also might impact the Athletics’ willingness to consider trade possibilities.  That said, one would also imagine clubs wouldn’t be willing to trade for Wilson without a long look at his medicals in the wake of his surgery.

The sixth overall pick of the 2023 draft, Wilson made his big league debut barely over a year after his draft date, and played in 28 games for the A’s during the 2024 campaign.  He then broke out by hitting .311/.355/.444 with 13 homers over 523 PA in 2025, finishing second in AL Rookie of the Year voting and also earning some down-ballot MVP votes.  Luis Arraez is the most frequent comp for Wilson’s game, as Wilson rarely strikes out and makes a ton of contact, even if he doesn’t often make hard contact.

Defensively, Wilson’s glovework drew below-average grades in 2025, and the Defensive Runs Saved gave him a -6 mark in 2026.  The Outs Above Average metric was much more favorable, as Wilson went from -3 OAA in 2025 (over 1053 2/3 innings at shortstop) to +9 (over 637 1/3 innings) in 2026.  These defensive questions could be a moot point if top shortstop prospect Leo De Vries lives up to expectations and Wilson is shifted over to second or third base, though De Vries’ timeline has been delayed by a shoulder surgery of his own, and is expected to be out until at least May 2027.

Moving Wilson would create another hole in the A’s infield and less of a safety net for De Vries’ eventual arrival in the majors.  That said, Smith could acquire a veteran shortstop as a stopgap, or use an internal option like Joshua Kuroda-Grauer or Alika Williams.  Offering Wilson could potentially help the Athletics land a much-needed dose of young pitching help, and maybe also a veteran pitcher on a larger salary to offset part of Wilson’s $66MM price tag.  It isn’t exactly a “bad contract swap” situation given Wilson’s youth and future potential, though his salary does create another obstacle in any trade talks the A’s could explore.

While a Wilson trade seems unlikely, Smith may have to resort to creative tactics in order to upgrade the Athletics’ pitching in both the short and long term.  Free agents obviously aren’t exactly rushing to spend time in Sacramento’s hitter-friendly ballpark, and it remains to be seen if the Athletics’ new home in Las Vegas might also favor batters.

title: Robert Griffin III counters Desmond Howard over Jeremiah Smith’s Heisman case: ‘Stop hating’
content:
Two of the most prominent Heisman Trophy winners in college football media are going at it over the favorite for this year’s award, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

Earlier this week in an appearance on ESPN’s First Take, Desmond Howard questioned Smith’s ability to make a “difference” in “the biggest games.” Howard argued that the case against Smith winning the Heisman went deeper than Ohio State losing its starting quarterback to injury, and that Smith did not have enough superstar “moments” to deserve the award.

Many raised an eyebrow at Howard’s impassioned argument against Smith — widely seen as the best player in college football this year — because Howard is an alum of Ohio State’s rival, Michigan.

The comments clearly drew a reaction across the media as well. During Fox’s broadcast of Ohio State-Northwestern on Saturday, game analyst and former Baylor star Robert Griffin III addressed Howard directly, calling on the College GameDay panelist to “stop hating” and uphold his place in the “Heisman brotherhood.”

“When you talk about the Heisman Trophy, my guy Desmond Howard, he’s been very critical of Jeremiah Smith and said, ‘When does this guy ever show up in big-time games?'” Griffin said on the call. “Well, he’s shown up in big-time games all over the place, and Desmond Howard has to stop hating on Jeremiah Smith just because he goes to Ohio State. That’s not the right way to do this, and we’ve got to be better in our Heisman brotherhood.”

https://t.co/PIzpzIJyiT

— welovesports40 (@welovesports40) November 14, 2026

Separate from his bias as a Michigan man, Howard’s criticism of Smith doesn’t really hold up. Smith caught eight passes for 144 yards in last year’s No. 1 vs. No. 2 bout in the Big Ten championship game, and then went for 157 yards and a touchdown in the College Football Playoff quarters. This season, Smith caught eight balls for 164 yards and a score early on against Texas, and broke the 200-yard mark with two touchdowns against Iowa three weeks later. Even as the Buckeyes dropped back-to-back games to USC and Oregon, Smith broke 80 yards and scored in each game.

While Griffin certainly relishes conflict with other media figures, it’s not hard to see why he called Howard out in this case. Howard took a cheap shot at a gifted and promising young star, making poor use of his immense platform on ESPN. And as a top analyst at Fox, which airs just about every Ohio State game, it is no surprise that Griffin would defend the program and its best player.

title: NL East Notes: Braves, Iglesias, Nationals, Thompson, Marlins
content:
The Braves made a big new bullpen addition by signing Evan Phillips on Thursday, and the Tigers just added a prominent high-leverage reliever in Emilio Pagan.  Even after these moves, reporter Francys Romero writes that Atlanta and Detroit are still interested in veteran closer Raisel Iglesias.  For the Braves, it would mark the second straight offseason they’ve re-signed Iglesias, after re-upping with the righty on a one-year, $16MM pact.

Obviously there’s plenty of familiarity between the two sides, and Iglesias has continue to pitch so well that there isn’t much concern of a slowdown even after he enters his age-37 season.  The Athletic’s Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal note that re-signing Iglesias to strengthen the bullpen would increase the chance that the Braves will use Didier Fuentes as a starter next season, though Atlanta figures to add a more proven starter even if Fuentes is indeed stretched out in Spring Training.

More from around the NL East…

  • The Nationals had one of baseball’s worst bullpens in 2026, but while improving the relief corps is an obvious offseason goal, “relievers who command multiple years and significant money are probably off the table,” the Athletic’s Spencer Nusbaum writes.  Since even contending teams often take this stance in acquiring relief help, it isn’t too surprising that the still-rebuilding Nats aren’t being too aggressive in adding the bullpen problem, even if Washington did exceed expectations with 77 wins last year.  The rotation also needs help, and to this end D.C. seems more aggressive, as Nusbaum said the Nats have “asked around about controllable starting pitching in trade talks, and is casting a wider net than last season.”
  • In other Nationals news, Nusbaum reports that the team has hired John Morris as the team’s new VP of baseball research.  The role puts Morris in charge of “the baseball side of the Nats analytics department,” as per Nusbaum.  Morris comes to Washington from New York, where he worked as the Yankees’ assistant director of quantitative analysis.
  • The Marlins have hired Trayce Thompson for a role in their baseball operations department, the Miami Herald’s Barry Jackson reports.  The news presumably means the 35-year-old Thompson is retiring after a pro career that saw him play in parts of seven MLB seasons from 2015-23, and Thompson has spent the last three years in the minors, the Mexican League, in independent baseball, and playing for Great Britain’s World Baseball Classic team.  Thompson played for five different clubs at the MLB level, with 217 of his 369 career games coming in a Dodgers uniform.  The ex-outfielder’s best sustained offensive performance was a second-half surge with the 2022 Dodgers, and Thompson will finish his career with 45 homers and a .212/.300/.411 slash line in 1058 plate appearances in the bigs.  MLB Trade Rumors congratulates Thompson on a fine career, and we wish him with the best as he begins this new direction in his baseball life.

title: How Much Is Wisconsin Coach Luke Fickell's Buyout? Contract Details In 2026
content: Luke Fickell jumped out of the Cincinnati frying pan straight into the Big Ten fire, and the Wisconsin Badgers are the ones who have been burned. Rather than elevating the program as promised, Fickell has stumbled to a 23-25 start as of 2026's Week 11 with the Badgers. With back-to-back losing seasons, the program has hit a low point it hasn't seen since Barry Alvarez's team in 2001. For 22 straight seasons, Wisconsin football was defined by winning records, Big Ten titles, and annual bowl trips. NIL may have reshaped college football, but that’s no excuse to abandon Wisconsin’s football identity. Fickell’s transition hasn't just been rocky; back-to-back losing seasons mark a drought the program hasn't experienced since the 1991 and 1992 seasons. This is the current state of Wisconsin football under Fickell. Given the sheer lack of results, his seat is scorching hot heading into a make-or-break season for the Badgers. An expanded roster budget only amplifies the pressure on Fickell and his coaching staff to show clear progress. If not, this could be his final season in Madison. With new athletics director Shawn Eichorst now at the helm, moving on from Fickell is financially far less complicated than it was a year ago. What Is Luke Fickell's 2026 Salary? Fickell is under contract through 2032 and set to make $7.8 million this season, ranking him in the top 25 nationally, according to USA TODAY's college football coaches salary database. But sitting right in the middle of the Big Ten salary stack is a far cry from his actual on-field production. How Much Is Fickell’s Buyout After This Season? According to reporting from The Athletic, Fickell’s buyout drops to $19.2 million after this season. While that remains a steep price for Eichorst to navigate, it is a manageable hit for a program of Wisconsin’s size if Fickell fails to turn things around in Madison. Can Fickell Earn Any Bonuses This Season? If Fickell can turn things around in Madison, he stands to benefit financially. According to USA TODAY's college football coaches salary database, he can earn up to $1.45 million in incentives if Wisconsin qualifies for the College Football Playoff and makes a deep postseason run. Who Are Wisconsin Coaching Replacement Options? If Wisconsin decides to fire Fickell at some point, it won't have to look far for replacements. Plenty of realistic options have deep ties to Madison, including three current FBS head coaches who would be natural fits for the program. At the top of the list is former Badger Jason Eck. After leaving his mark at Idaho, he took over last season at New Mexico and immediately put together a 9-4 record, nearly pushing the Lobos into the Mountain West conference championship game. Should Eck continue his winning ways at New Mexico, he could be a natural target for the Badgers. A La Crosse native, Eck played offensive line for Wisconsin under Alvarez from 1995 to 1998 before starting his coaching career as a graduate assistant for the program in 1999. Dickert might be comfortable with the Demon Deacons, but the Badgers could be intriguing enough to lure him away from the ACC. Coming off an impressive 9-4 first season, Dickert’s stock continues to rise. Not only does Dickert have the coaching resume to support a move to the Big Ten, but his deep roots in the state are hard to ignore. Having grown up in Oconto, Wisconsin, and played college football at UW-Stevens Point, local recruiting won’t be an issue. After leaving Washington State for Wake Forest, speculation quickly began about when Dickert might make another jump toward the Big Ten or even the SEC. He has overachieved at every stop and if Wisconsin wants to take a chance, he could be a natural fit. With North Dakota State officially making the leap to the Mountain West after two decades of dominating the FCS, the Bison are finally in the FBS. Head coach Tim Polasek has the program primed to prove it belongs from day one. Polasek has posted a 27-3 record with the Bison since taking over from Matt Entz, capped by an FCS national championship in his very first season. If Wisconsin ever wanted to take an untraditional route and look for a hidden gem, landing a native Badger state product like Polasek could make a lot of sense. It also helps that Polasek also has deep Wisconsin ties. He grew up in Iola, Wisconsin and played quarterback for Concordia University Wisconsin, and coached at Wisconsin–Stevens Point from 2003 to 2005. If he were to ever leave the Bison, an opportunity in Madison could be hard to pass up.

title: Tom Brady Opens Up About 'Complicated' Relationship With Michigan
content: Tom Brady's relationship with Michigan has never been particularly straightforward. But there's no denying the role Michigan played in shaping the person and player he ultimately became. In a first-look teaser for FOX Sports' upcoming two-part documentary, "The Team: Michigan Football," released Saturday during "Big Noon Kickoff," Brady offered a reflection on his time in Ann Arbor. "If I look back on Michigan, that wasn't the choice," Brady says in the teaser. "I went to a place that there was no guaranteed success. If anything, when I look back, I was guaranteeing a lot of hardships." Brady left his hometown of San Mateo, California, in 1995, to play for a Michigan program that already had a crowded quarterback room. He redshirted during his freshman year and spent the next two seasons as a backup, watching Brian Griese lead the Wolverines to an undefeated season and a share of the national championship in 1997. Brady would go on to finish his college career with a 20-5 record as a starter, including wins in the Citrus Bowl and Orange Bowl, but it wasn't always easy. Those challenges were central to the person he became. "Do I look back and wish I would have changed anything? No, not at all," Brady said in the clip. "Is my relationship with Michigan a little bit complicated? Yeah. It definitely is." "From age 17 to when I walked on the campus to when I left, those 4.5 years really shaped who I was as a person," he added. "It really defined who I could be going forward." Executive produced by Brady and former Michigan head coach Jim Harbaugh, "The Team: Michigan Football" will offer a deeper look at the program's history and legacy. Part 1 premieres Friday, Nov. 27, at 7 p.m. ET on FOX, the night before Michigan and Ohio State meet in "The Game" on "Big Noon Saturday." Part 2 will air Saturday, Dec. 12, at 6:30 p.m. ET. title: Mauricio Pochettino Tracker: Man United Makes It Official, Is Pep Open To USA Job?
content: It's official: Mauricio Pochettino is leaving the U.S. men’s national team. On Friday, a day after Manchester United fired Michael Carrick, the 20-time English champions named Pochettino as his replacement, with the club currently in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of its first 10 matches to begin the season. The 54-year-old Argentine will lead the Americans for two final games, on Saturday and Tuesday vs. Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals, before taking over the Red Devils in time for Sunday's trip to rivals Liverpool. Pochettino signed a contract extension with U.S. Soccer in August that runs through the 2030 World Cup, following the USA’s run to the round of 16 at the 2026 event. To get him out of that deal, United triggered a buyout clause reportedly worth nearly $10 million. Pochettino's assistant coaches, including longtime top deputy Jesus Perez, will follow him to Old Trafford. "The club has reached an agreement with the U.S. Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the U.S. Men’s National Team," Manchester United said as part of their announcement, which said he'll formally take over the Red Devils on Nov. 18. In 35 games at the American helm, the former Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur and Southampton manager posted a record of 21W-11L-2T. Three of those victories came at the 2026 World Cup, making Pochettino the winningest USA men's coach at soccer's marquee tournament. U.S. Soccer now needs a new coach for the 2030 cycle. Here are the top candidates to replace him. "Mauricio has left a lasting mark on U.S. Soccer through his leadership, professionalism and commitment to our players and culture," U.S. Soccer CEO JT Batson said in a press release. "He and his staff raised standards, strengthened our culture and created clearer connections from the youth national teams to the senior team. Those changes are now embedded in how we operate, and we will keep building on them as we pursue sustained success on the world stage." Saturday, Nov. 14 With the U.S. men's national team taking on Haiti in Miami in the first match of the two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal series, the chatter will already turn to who will replace Mauricio Pochettino. And the early focus will be on one big name: Pep Guardiola. According to a report from talkSPORT on Saturday, U.S. Soccer will begin "initial negotiations" with Guardiola next week following Pochettino's decision to leave the U.S. men's national team for Manchester United. The 55-year-old Guardiola has one of the best résumés on hand and would easily be the top pick for just about any club or country. He coached Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City. At Barça, he led a squad with legends like Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta, and Xavi Hernandez to three La Liga and two Champions League crowns. After a successful stint at Bayern (albiet with no Champions Leeague titles), he took over at City in 2016 – which included six Premier League titles and the club's first ever Champions League trophy in 2023. Friday, Nov. 13 The tears welled in Mauricio Pochettino’s eyes as Manchester United’s new manager formally bid farewell to the U.S. Soccer Federation and its men’s national team on Friday. A little more than two hours after USSF and 20-time English champions announced that Pochettino would succeed Michael Carrick with the struggling Premier League titans, Pochettino took the stage inside U.S. Soccer’s training facility outside Atlanta to explain his decision to leave just three months into a contract that was supposed to run through the 2030 World Cup — a decision he called "one of the most difficult" of his 17-year coaching career. "It's difficult now to talk," Pochettino said, struggling to compose himself while flanked by U.S. Soccer CEO JT Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone. "I am a very emotional guy." As part of the agreement with United, Pochettino will oversee two final games with the U.S. before starting his new job in Manchester on Nov. 18. The Stars and Stripes meet Haiti on Saturday in Miami in the opening leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal series before the decisive second match in Cincinnati on Tuesday. Pochettino informed his players and the national team’s support staff later Thursday that he was leaving. "It all was so quick," he said. Thursday, Nov. 12 According to The Athletic, Pochettino would sign a 2.5-year deal that would run through summer 2029. There are details that are still being finalized but the deal would allow Pochettino to coach the U.S. in the next two games against Haiti before jetting off to Manchester.And what would be Pochettino's first game as Manchester United's first coach? Ancient rivals Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22 on the other end of the current international break. The first step in Pochettino potentially taking over at Old Trafford has been completed. Michael Carrick was fired by Manchester United on Thursday after overseeing the 20-time English champion’s worst start to a Premier League season. Carrick’s departure comes less than six months after he was given a two-year contract and the responsibility of reviving the fortunes of the once-dominant force of English soccer. United hasn’t won the league since managerial great Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. According to ESPN, Manchester United execs have informed U.S. Soccer that they intend to trigger the $10 million (£7m) release clause in Pochettino's contract. Pochettino is currently with the USMNT team at U.S. Soccer’s training center outside of Atlanta before opening their two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal series against Haiti, with the first game set for Saturday in Miami. The second game will be next Tuesday in Cincinnati. Pochettino is expected to remain with the U.S. players for these games regardless of what decision is made about the Man United vacancy. Several USA players spoke highly about Pochettino after team training on Thursday. "Poch has definitely raised the standard since he's been in charge," striker Folarin Balogun said Thursday, who led the U.S. with three goals in four World Cup appearances, including game-winners over Paraguay and Bosnia and Herzegovina. "The intensity of training, how we approach games — he's changed our way of thinking as players. "He's laid the foundation," Balogun continued. "I think we have the ownership as players to carry that on." Wednesday, Nov. 11 Whatever happens with Manchester United, Pochettino is expected to remain on the U.S. sideline for at least two more matches. Pochettino is in camp with the team at U.S. Soccer’s National Training Center in Fayetteville, Georgia, preparing for the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti on Saturday in Miami and Tuesday in Cincinnati. He’s expected to speak to the media Friday, per his usual pre-match routine. United have not yet officially fired Carrick or made formal contact with U.S. Soccer about Pochettino’s contract. The club has the rest of the international break to finalize a replacement before returning to action at Liverpool on Nov. 22. U.S. Soccer is expected to make Pep Guardiola a top target to replace Pochettino if he leaves, according to The Athletic. The former Manchester City manager has had past conversations with the federation and has long been intrigued by the idea of working in the United States. United have not yet officially fired Carrick or made formal contact with U.S. Soccer about Pochettino. He’s expected to coach the USA in its Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal matches against Haiti on Saturday in Miami and Tuesday in Cincinnati. If U.S. Soccer goes with an American, no one has a stronger case right now than B.J. Callaghan. He led Nashville SC to a league-record point total in the MLS regular season and already has experience in charge of the U.S. men’s national team, guiding the team to the 2023 Concacaf Nations League title as interim coach. The Nashville SC coach is coming off one of the greatest regular seasons in MLS history. Nashville went 23-3-8 in 2026 and finished with 77 points, breaking Inter Miami’s single-season record of 74 set in 2024. Along the way, Callaghan’s team won the club’s first Supporters’ Shield, finished a record 13 points clear of the next-best team and set MLS records for wins, fewest losses (3) and fewest goals allowed (25). Nashville also reached the Concacaf Champions Cup semifinals this year and became the first MLS team to win at Mexico City’s Estadio Azteca, beating Club América 1-0 in the quarterfinals. The turnaround has been remarkable. When Callaghan took over in July 2024, Nashville was in the middle of the worst season in its MLS history. Two years later, it’s one of the most dominant teams in the league. If U.S. Soccer wants a candidate with deep roots in the program, few fit better than Michael Bradley. The former U.S. men’s national team captain earned 151 caps for his country, many of them under his father, Bob Bradley, who coached the national team from 2006 to 2011. Michael’s coaching career is still young. He led Red Bull New York’s reserve team to the 2025 MLS Next Pro title in his first season as a head coach, then took over the first team ahead of the 2026 season. His résumé is thin compared to the other names on this list, but his knowledge of the American player pool and his reputation as a leader make him an intriguing long-term option. If U.S. Soccer wants a coach who already knows the program’s next generation, Cherundolo is already working with it. The federation hired Cherundolo in July to lead the U.S. under-23 team through the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, a role designed to work closely with the senior and youth national team staffs. He’s currently overseeing the team’s first camp of the Olympic cycle in Spain, where the U-23s are facing Scotland and Ukraine. That makes him a natural successor to Pochettino, and he’d already have relationships with many of the young players expected to push for spots in 2030. His coaching résumé also stands up. In four seasons at LAFC from 2022 to 2025, Cherundolo went 106-55-32 and never finished worse than third in the Western Conference. He won the MLS Cup and Supporters’ Shield in his first season and added the U.S. Open Cup in 2024. Few coaches have done more with less in MLS than Nancy, and that track record could make him a strong fit for international soccer. The 49-year-old Frenchman built his reputation at CF Montréal, where he won the 2021 Canadian Championship and led the club to the second-best record in MLS in 2022. That earned him a move to the Columbus Crew, where he became one of the league’s most respected coaches. Nancy led Columbus to the 2023 MLS Cup in his first season, then won the 2024 Leagues Cup and was named MLS Coach of the Year. The big question mark is his short stint at Celtic. Nancy left Columbus to take over the Scottish club in December 2025, but he was fired after just 33 days, having won only two of his eight matches. His MLS résumé is still among the best of any coach on this list, and his familiarity with North American soccer could be an asset. Martinez has experience managing teams on the international stage. He coached Belgium from 2016 to 2022, guiding its golden generation to a third-place finish at the 2018 World Cup, then took over Portugal in 2023. He stepped down after Portugal’s 1-0 loss to Spain in the round of 16 at this summer’s World Cup, saying he came to win the tournament and saw no point in continuing after falling short. Before his international career, Martinez won the 2013 FA Cup with Wigan Athletic and managed Everton. Now available, the 53-year-old Spaniard would bring proven international experience to a program looking to make a deep run in 2030.

Paul Finebaum eviscerates Oklahoma AD, defends SEC over Ole Miss postponement
content:
The game between the Oklahoma Sooners and Ole Miss Rebels is the only major college football contest shifted to Sunday in the wake of the FAA ground stop affecting flights across the nation.

While several games had to adjust start times, Ole Miss was seemingly the only one that couldn’t make it to their destination in time to play the game on Saturday. The situation drew a strong rebuke from Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny. He issued a blistering statement about the postponement, even saying that the SEC threatened the school with a forfeit if they didn’t agree to the rescheduling.

It’s clear Oklahoma is unhappy because of the logistics of the move and the impact it will have on its fans planning to attend or watch the game. And maybe it is peculiar that Ole Miss is the only school unable to travel to keep the game on Saturday and didn’t want to take a long bus ride to make it happen on schedule.

But on SEC Nation, Paul Finebaum had no sympathy for the Sooners. In fact, he stuck up for the SEC and commissioner Greg Sankey and had strong words for Denny for not thinking of the conference as a whole and everyone else who had to navigate unprecedented circumstances.

Paul Finebaum: “I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss… What I don’t think is correct is [Oklahoma AD Roger Denny] pathetically pandering to his fanbase at midnight to try to cover up whatever…” https://t.co/k124Yv7Ocq

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 14, 2026

“I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss. But I believe the administration and Ole Miss did everything they could. What I don’t think is correct is Roger Denny, the athletic director there, pathetically pandering to his fanbase at midnight to try to cover up whatever, I don’t know,” Finebaum said.

“Mr. Denny, the commissioner of the Southeastern Conference made a decision for the entire conference and for the safety of everyone. He’s not concerned about what you’re doing with your fanbase. And what Roger Denny has been doing all this year is pandering to his fanbase.”

Finebaum then cited Denny giving head coach Brent Venables a contract extension and underperforming this season, far away from College Football Playoff contention. He then called Denny an “impulsive leader” and even noted his former career as a tax attorney. In saying Oklahoma runs differently than other programs in the conference, he then added that it was “against the code of the SEC.”

“What he did here is really against the code of the SEC to call out a commissioner during a national crisis and emergency. He’s thinking about himself and his fanbase, who’s already on tenderhooks because of the season, and I think he is dead wrong and quite frankly, I think it’s unbecoming of a leader in college athletics or anywhere to do what he did,” Finebaum added.

It’s interesting that Paul Finebaum would reference the “code” of the SEC in the same week that commissioner Greg Sankey called out ESPN announcers for not showing enough deference to the league’s officials. We’ll see if the whole saga provides Oklahoma with some added motivation for the game on Sunday if they feel like the entire SEC machine has turned against them.

title: Haaland Scores Late Penalty To Seal Norway's Nations League Win Over Wales
content: Erling Haaland ended a two-game run without scoring for Norway with the third goal in a 3-1 victory over Wales in the Nations League in Oslo on Saturday. The 26-year-old Manchester City star looked set to go three games without scoring – an anomaly for a player who averages at least one goal for every international match he plays – until Connor Roberts conceded a penalty with a foul on Andreas Schjelderup in the 85th minute. Haaland stayed cool while the decision survived a VAR check, then swung his spot kick to the right of Wales goalkeeper Karl Darlow. He almost got a second in stoppage time but had to be content with his tally of 66 goals in 60 appearances for Norway – extending his national record. Haaland’s rate of scoring is unseen since "der Bomber" Gerd Muller scored 68 in 62 games for West Germany, including the decisive goal in the 1974 World Cup final. Norway needed Antonio Nusa to get the breakthrough in the 59th after Wales’ defense failed to adequately clear a corner. Haaland set up Schjelderup to make it 2-0 with a simple finish soon after, only for David Brooks to make the finish exciting with a brilliant chip over the goalkeeper. Haaland then ended any suspense to seal Norway's second win in Group A4. Reporting by The Associated Press.

Guardiola, who won 41 trophies during his 19 years managing in Europe, has been a highly-coveted free agent since stepping down as Manchester City's manager in May 2026. If the U.S. manages to sign Guardiola, he will immediately become the biggest head coach in international soccer, despite never coaching a national team before. Pochettino, notably, also never coached a national team before taking the U.S. job in 2024. Pochettino will coach the U.S. through its Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal matches vs. Haiti this week. After that, he will leave for Manchester and the U.S. head coaching job will be vacant. title: Dodgers Interested In Jonathan Loaisiga, Tim Hill
content:
Right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga and left-hander Tim Hill are two of the relievers on the Dodgers’ radar, according to (respectively) ESPN’s Jesse Rogers and the New York Post’s Jon Heyman.  Rogers notes that Loaisiga is “getting closer” to landing a deal, so a signing might come sooner rather than later.

Beyond Los Angeles, Loaisiga and Hill have also each drawn interest from the Yankees (their mutual former team) and Mets.  The Blue Jays have been linked to Loaisiga as well, and Rogers suggests that at least one other team is also in on the right-hander.  The Guardians, Giants, and Cardinals have all been linked to Hill in previous reports.

For Loaisiga in particular, this healthy market is a terrific outcome for a pitcher who had to settle for a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks last winter.  The righty had shown flashes of being an elite relief arm during his eight seasons with the Yankees, yet injuries continually kept Loaisiga on the sidelines.  New York declined a $5MM club option on Loaisiga after the 2025 season, and he was both healthy and very effective in delivering a 2.42 ERA over 67 innings out of Arizona’s pen in 2026.

While Loaisiga doesn’t rack up many strikeouts, he induces a ton of grounders and a lot of soft contact, plus he has a strong 6.3% walk rate in 260 innings since the start of the 2020 season.  MLB Trade Rumors ranked Loaisiga 45th on our top 50 free agents list and projected a two-year, $13MM contract, making him a potential bargain for a lot of teams provided the 32-year-old can again avoid the injury bug.

Now entering his age-37 season, Hill has a similar resume as a grounder-heavy control pitcher who rarely records strikeouts.  Hill has continued to dominate left-handed batters but righties hit him pretty well, and a big spike in his home run totals led to Hill’s 4.60 ERA over 58 2/3 innings for the Yankees last season.  Hill is the type of reliever who would’ve held more appeal prior to the introduction of the three-batter rule, but the veteran is still a logical target for clubs in need of left-handed bullpen help.

The Dodgers have hopes of re-signing Alex Vesia, and Tanner Scott, Justin Wrobleski, and Jack Dreyer are among the left-handed bullpen options remaining on the L.A. roster.  Still, Hill would further bolster this group, and it’s not hard to imagine the Dodgers adding both Hill and Loaisiga as part of their goal of amassing pitching for another extended playoff run.  The right-handed side of the Los Angeles pen took a hit when Evan Phillips signed with the Braves, perhaps increasing the Dodgers’ interest in Loaisiga.

title: TKO CEO Ari Emanuel blames Pete Buttigieg for FAA shutdown
content:
Ari Emanuel has a lot on his plate as the CEO of TKO Group and Hollywood superagent. But he had plenty of time to make a statement about the FAA grounding all flights nationwide after a technological malfunction on Friday.

But in a post on social media, Emanuel had a strange target for his anger — former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg.

Buttigieg served in the role under President Joe Biden but hasn’t been in office since January 2025 when Donald Trump emerged victorious in the 2024 election and his administration took over. Sean Duffy has been in the role since then and has had his own fair share of controversies under his watch, including the chaos that developed over the weekend. At a press conference about the outage, Duffy’s performance was widely panned by people of all political stripes for his lack of leadership.

However, Emanuel saw it was Buttigieg’s fault for not installing enough modern upgrades during his time as secretary. Interestingly, he had nothing to say about the current administration’s role.

No one’s hands are clean here. However, Mr. Secretary Buttigieg, you had four years in the job and infrastructure money, yet made zero progress modernizing the FAA. You left a failing system in place. THANKS!

— Ari Emanuel (@AriEmanuel) November 13, 2026

“No one’s hands are clean here. However, Mr. Secretary Buttigieg, you had four years in the job and infrastructure money, yet made zero progress modernizing the FAA. You left a failing system in place. THANKS!” Emanuel wrote.

Emanuel’s comments are peculiar given his TKO company has been under fire for their travel policies and business with Saudi Arabia. WWE just held a show in Riyadh around various missile attacks on the city, and employees are starting to speak up about how the company does not care for them and only values profit and greed.

The criticism is also surprising because Emanuel has been a prominent supporter of Barack Obama and longtime Democratic advocate. Of course, his brother Rahm served as White House Chief of Staff under President Obama and also as a Democrat in the House of Representatives and as Mayor of Chicago.

However, in spite of his left-leaning political interests and longtime Democratic party support, Ari Emanuel’s agency represented Donald Trump during his time on The Apprentice. And when Trump was first elected president, Ari Emanuel was reportedly vetted for a potential role in his administration. Just last month in an interview with PBS, Emanuel said he still talks to Trump and values the conversations outside an “echo chamber.”

As chairman of TKO, Ari Emanuel is also head of what stands as arguably the most pro-Trump sports league on the planet in UFC. Trump regularly attends UFC shows and is routinely celebrated by Dana White and many fighters. The MAGAfication of UFC peaked with an event at Trump’s White House this summer and the sitting president even (jokingly?) suggested White become his new press secretary. The ties between WWE and Trump also run deep with the McMahon family longtime friends and partners. Donald Trump is in the WWE Hall of Fame and Linda McMahon serves on Trump’s cabinet.

Having said all of that, it is odd to see Ari Emanuel condemn someone who hasn’t been in the job as Secretary of Transportation for two years, especially as it sounds like something you’d hear from conservative media. Blaming the Biden admin for issues like rising inflation and gas prices was a failed tactic for Republicans before the blue tsumani on Election Day 2026. It speaks to there being something potentially personal between Emanuel and Buttigieg that goes beyond your garden variety politics. Or maybe the political leanings of TKO are starting to rub off on their CEO.

title: Padres Interested In Freddy Peralta, Nick Martinez, Matthew Boyd
content:
The Padres have interest in free agent starters Freddy Peralta and Nick Martinez, according to ESPN’s Alden Gonzalez.  Matthew Boyd is another name of interest to the team, as per Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune, though Acee notes that the Padres have “showed some level of interest in virtually every starting pitcher on the market….rather than list the starters whose representatives the Padres talked to, suffice it to say there is hardly a starting pitcher they are not considering.”

The rotation push is understandable given that Michael King, Nick Pivetta, Walker Buehler, Casey Mize, Robbie Ray, and Griffin Canning are all free agents.  This leaves San Diego with a current starting staff of Randy Vasquez, JP Sears, Joe Musgrove (who may be used in the bullpen), newly-signed swingman candidate Ryan Weiss, and maybe Yu Darvish, if the veteran still wants to continue his career.

Suffice it to say, the Padres need to fill at least four and maybe five rotation spots this winter, leaving the team searching every corner of the starting pitching market (and undoubtedly the trade market as well).  Peralta, Martinez, and Boyd represent a range of starters and potential price points for the Friars.  On our list of the offseason’s top 50 free agents, MLBTR projected Peralta for a five-year, $110MM contract, Martinez for two years and $42MM, and Boyd for a one-year, $13MM deal.

Peralta’s final price tag will be particularly interesting to gauge, as the right-hander struggled with the Mets before regaining his old form after a deadline trade to the Rays.  The possibility exists that a straight five-year, nine-figure commitment won’t be there for Peralta if teams are wary about his extended cold stretch in New York, which might present an opening for a creative executive like Padres president of baseball operations A.J. Preller.  The Padres’ past deals with the likes of King and Pivetta included opt-outs, so it could be that Peralta might be open to such an early off-ramp in order to re-enter the market on the strength of a stronger platform year.

Martinez is no stranger to these types of Padres contracts, as he signed two different deals with San Diego after returning to the majors from a four-year stint in Japan from 2018-21.  Martinez worked as both a starter and reliever over two seasons with the Padres, and 2026 marked the first time in his nine MLB seasons that the right-hander worked exclusively as a starter.  The result was a very solid season in Tampa Bay’s rotation, setting Martinez up for a multi-year deal even though he is already 36 years old.

Boyd is also entering his age-36 season, and he missed some time due to arthroscopic knee surgery in 2026.  The southpaw has a lengthy health history but (last year’s meniscus tear aside) he has been generally healthier over the past two seasons with the Cubs, delivering a 3.50 ERA over 306 1/3 innings.  Boyd projects as a third starter type at best, but that would be fine for the Padres if they can land some other frontline arms who are clearer candidates to start a playoff game.

After evaluating many options during the GM Meetings, Preller told Acee and other reporters that he’d be speaking this coming week with new owners Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones plus team CEO Erik Greupner to discuss the Padres’ spending capacity.  “Jose and Kwanza are open to having those conversations, open to what that means from a different dollar amount and different contract commitments, and hopefully we make some good decisions,” Preller said.

As Feliciano and Jones enter their first full season in charge of the club, Acee writes that the duo plan to spend at least as much on payroll as in 2026, and for San Diego to be at least a top-10 payroll club.  MLBTR’s Payroll Tracker calculates the Padres’ approximate $224MM payroll in 2026 as ninth in the league, with a luxury tax number of roughly $269.4MM that sat sixth among all teams.

Looking ahead to next year, San Diego has a little over $193MM on the books and a tax number of around $192.6MM, which allows Preller for some flexibility.  To some extent, Feliciano and Jones may feel compelled to increase spending out of sheer need, given the Padres’ needs in not just the rotation, but also in the bullpen and a couple of lineup holes.

Turning to the relief corps, Acee writes that the Padres had some interest in Evan Phillips before the right-hander signed a three-year, $35MM contract with the Braves.  The Friars saw plenty of Phillips during his six seasons with the Dodgers, and if nothing else, the Padres will be glad to see him out of the NL West — Phillips has a sparkling 1.19 ERA over 22 2/3 career innings against San Diego.

title: ‘College GameDay’ returns to Army-Navy Game for first time since 2023
content:
College GameDay is making its first appearance at the famed Army-Navy Game for the first time in multiple years.

The flagship ESPN college football program has had on and off appearances at the standalone contest over the years. The last time it made the visit was in 2023 when the game took place in Foxborough, Massachusetts.

This year the Army-Navy Game will be at Metlife Stadium in the Meadowlands for the 127th edition of the classic rivalry on December 12. With the expansion of the College Football Playoff, the game will move up a week next year and maintain its standalone date in 2027.

ESPN made the announcement of its latest visit on Saturday morning during the College GameDay live show in Boise State.

GameDay has come under scrutiny like never before with the outsized presence of Pat McAfee transforming the beloved institution and becoming the show’s centerpiece, whether fans like it or not. There’s also the backdrop of ESPN’s mega-contract with the SEC and the show being questioned for repeatedly returning to the same venues multiple times. Some of that criticism has extended to the content of the show, which has been severely lacking in anything substantive outside the SEC and Big Ten.

However, it seems like College GameDay has at least heard some of those criticisms and made a conscious effort to cast a wider net across college football in recent weeks. In fact, the show hasn’t visited an SEC school since all the way back on October 10 at Alabama. Recent stops have included BYU, Utah, and Boise State.

The Army-Navy Game has drawn some of its biggest viewership numbers ever over the past couple of years on CBS. You can certainly make the argument that College GameDay should make the trip every year. And whatever playoff implications may or may not be on the line, it’s a game that has always mattered a great deal to college football and American sports as a whole.

title: AL Central Notes: White Sox, Twins, Burg, Guardians
content:
The White Sox are focused on bolstering their rotation this winter, both with external additions and internal moves like moving Grant Taylor from the bullpen to a starting role.  Even with Taylor leaving the relief mix, however, GM Chris Getz downplayed the idea of prioritizing the bullpen when speaking with the Chicago Sun-Times’ James Fegan and other reporters.  Rather than invest heavily in relievers, the Sox could use any excess starters in bullpen roles, with perhaps a lower-cost veteran or two added later in the offseason for added depth.

Since the White Sox are so deep in infield prospects, it has been suggested that the club could trade from this depth to address other needs.  Getz didn’t rule this possibility out in the future, but it is “not something that I would say we’re entertaining right now.”  It’s a fair stance to take, as the Sox might not want to move any younger talent until they have a better idea of which of these infielders they view as true building blocks.  Despite Chicago’s unexpected AL Central title, the Sox aren’t going to pivot entirely away from their rebuilding plan, and the current infield grouping of Miguel Vargas, Colson Montgomery, Chase Meidroth, and Munetaka Murakami all contributed heavily to the playoff run.

More from around the AL Central…

  • The Twins have a significantly greater need in the bullpen than in the rotation, but could be taking somewhat of the same approach as the White Sox to the relief corps.  Minnesota could look to add to its rotation (probably more of a mid-rotation type) and then use at least one of the leftover starters to fill a hole in the bullpen, The Athletic’s Dan Hayes writes, since the Twins have traditionally never been eager about spending much money on relief pitching.  GM Jeremy Zoll acknowledged that his team would “need to be open-minded to” potential rotation adds, “knowing that it feels like an area of surplus but also want to be mindful of not eating into that too much since we know we’re going to need real depth to attack the season.”  Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley, and the returning Pablo Lopez line up as the projected top three in Minnesota’s rotation, with Dean Kremer, Zebby Matthews, Bailey Ober, Connor Prielipp, and Mick Abel all competing for the final two slots.
  • The Guardians are hiring Alex Burg as their new quality control coach, Justice delos Santos of the Bay Area News Group reports.  Burg has been on the Giants’ coaching staff for the last five seasons, working as a bullpen coach in 2022-23, the catching coach for the last three seasons, and he was also San Francisco’s Major League field coordinator this past year.  In between the end of his nine-year minor league career and the start of his tenure with the Giants, Burg also spent three years on the Rangers’ staff.

title: Aaron Rodgers shares heartfelt picture with Jordan Rodgers after family reconciliation
content:
After years of a public family feud, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers appears to have fully reconciled with his brother and ESPN analyst Jordan Rodgers.

The elder Rodgers has made headlines over the years for his complex relationships regarding his family and various love interests. The rift became public when younger brother Jordan appeared on Season 12 of The Bachelorette in 2016. It was revealed that Aaron Rodgers was no longer on speaking terms with his family, including his brother.

While it was thought that actress Olivia Munn and her relationship with Aaron Rodgers could have been at the center of the breakdown of the family dynamic, he insisted that there were deep-rooted issues in the Rodgers clan.

But earlier this year, things suddenly began to change. In July, Aaron Rodgers posted a picture of himself with his parents and other family members, signaling that the longstanding feud had come to an end and that there had been a reconciliation. However, Jordan Rodgers was absent from the photos.

But with Jordan Rodgers in Pittsburgh on Friday night with ESPN to call a college football game between the Pitt Panthers and Florida State Seminoles, Aaron Rodgers dropped by the broadcast booth to say hello. And the brothers posted a picture of their reunion to Instagram to signal to the world that all is now well with the family.

 

View this post on Instagram

 

A post shared by Aaron Rodgers (@aaronrodgers12)

“Great to see little bro @jrodgers11 in his element tonight @acrisurestadium. Really proud of how hard he’s worked to get to where he is now @pitt_fb @mikemonaco_.” Rodgers’ caption of the photo read.

Say what you will about Aaron Rodgers, his personal beliefs, and some of the decisions he’s made over the years. Rodgers is flying high with the Pittsburgh Steelers and now happily married. He credited his wife this offseason with helping the healing process and move forward. Latest On Ketel Marte
content:
Diamondbacks officials met with  Ketel Marte’s agent Charisse Espinosa-Dash during the GM Meetings this week, but the D’Backs “but did not seem to come away with a clear idea about what teams to which Marte would be willing to approve a deal,” the Arizona Republic’s Nick Piecoro writes.  Marte has full no-trade protection as a 10-and-5 player, so even though he is one of the offseason’s most prominent trade candidates, the possibility exists that Marte will remain in Arizona simply because he isn’t interested in changing teams.

It puts the D’Backs in something of an awkward position, especially since the impending lockout will interrupt all transactions activity for what could be months on end.  If Marte isn’t dealt by 10:59pm CT on December 1 (when the current collective bargaining agreement expires and the league is expected to lock out the players), the uncertainty over his future will continue to linger over all of the Diamondbacks’ remaining offseason plans.

As Piecoro puts it, “the Diamondbacks seem to have little choice but to sort of blindly attempt to make the best deal possible without knowing whether Marte will approve it.”  In terms of what that best deal might entail, Piecoro writes that the D’Backs have looked into all variety of trades in their early discussions about Marte — bringing in just prospects, swapping the second baseman for other established big league talents, or a trade package of both veteran and younger talent.

GM Mike Hazen naturally didn’t go into any detail about the Marte negotiations, but the executive expressed some regret at focusing on MLB-ready younger players in past trades of such star players as Zack Greinke or Paul Goldschmidt.  This could hint that Hazen is looking to add just the best talent available (whether that’s current big leaguers or longer-term prospects) while shopping Marte, which is probably a logical approach since Hazen’s options are already limited by Marte’s no-trade leverage.

One option still under consideration is moving Marte for another player on a hefty contract, for salary offset purposes.  The Diamondbacks “did not seem to be leaning in that direction,” as Piecoro says that Arizona’s preference would be to clear some of Marte’s remaining $91.75MM salary off the books and then reinvest that money into other roster needs.  That $91.75MM figure is a little higher than the $87.5MM owed to Marte in the initial terms of his contract, as Piecoro hears from a source that Marte unlocked incentive bonuses based on plate appearances.

The Blue Jays, Giants, Mariners, Phillies, Pirates, Rays, Red Sox, and Tigers all reportedly had some level of interest in Marte last offseason, and Toronto’s interest has continued into this winter.  As MLBTR’s Anthony Franco explored in a recent post about Marte’s potential market, Seattle, San Francisco, and Pittsburgh are probably out of the running based on various factors emerging within the last year.  There’s also the possibility that Marte’s infamous no-show of a game in Boston this past August might have put past suitors or any other teams off entirely.

title: Desmond Howard questions Heisman candidacy of Jeremiah Smith
content:
Jeremiah Smith may be the Heisman Trophy favorite at the moment, but the star wide receiver for the Ohio State Buckeyes is taking fire from both friends and enemies.

Smith somehow remains in the top spot in the Heisman rankings in spite of the disastrous nosedive of the Ohio State season and the pressure facing Ryan Day in Columbus. It all started spiraling after quarterback Julian Sayin went down with an injury against the Indiana Hoosiers. Day chose to go with true freshman Luke Fahey as the backup instead of five-star recruit Tavien St. Clair and the Buckeyes have lost consecutive games by double digits for the first time in years.

It was clear that Smith was visibly frustrated during OSU’s embarrassing home loss to Oregon. And he was controversially called a “petulant child” by beat writer Jeremy Birmingham. Now he’s receiving criticism from a place where you would more naturally suspect, a prominent Michigan alum.

ESPN College GameDay analyst Desmond Howard called out Jeremiah Smith on Friday for his lack of impact on the Buckeyes. Howard appeared on First Take and questioned the entirety of the Heisman field, saying that nobody has stood out yet for having a big moment in a big game. He would know that first-hand as his punt return touchdown against the Buckeyes in the biggest rivalry in the sport propelled his own campaign in 1991.

Desmond Howard on Jeremiah Smith

“When in the last two seasons has Jeremiah Smith been the difference in big games?”

Desmond says he hasn’t seen it yet.

We all know Jeremiah Smith is an incredible talent, but Desmond is questioning whether his impact in the biggest games matches the hype surrounding him.

The hype is generational. Desmond is asking where the generational moments are.

— Michigan Metal (@Metaleka_) November 13, 2026

“When you talk about Jeremiah, it’s more than just losing Julian Sayin. You’ve got to have those moments. In the last two years, give me one game where Jeremiah Smith, the wide receiver at Ohio State, was the difference in a big game in the last two years. This season and last season. Give me that game. As much as he puts up these magnificent numbers and these one-handed catches, I need moments against the top competition that makes me say ‘he was the guy,'” Howard said.

Desmond Howard hasn’t exactly been neutral in his commentary about Ohio State over the years as he routinely picks against the Buckeyes. That’s fine, it’s what rivalry is all about. In fact, it’s one of the reasons why Kirk Herbstreit isn’t as popular with Buckeye fans as Howard is with Wolverine fans. Herbstreit has gone to extreme lengths to project neutrality and criticized the Ohio State fanbase on multiple occasions.

But this commentary goes beyond rivalry trolling and makes you wonder what games Desmond Howard is watching. The two-year cutoff is convenient given Jeremiah Smith had 5 catches for 88 yards and a touchdown in a national championship game, including the game-clinching catch.

As for this season, before the Sayin injury, Smith put up spectacular numbers in Ohio State’s biggest games.

At #4 Texas, he put up 8 catches for 164 yards and a score before the team collapsed in the fourth quarter to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory.

Against #14 Iowa, he had 11 catches for 206 yards and a score.

Against #5 Indiana, he also led the Buckeyes with 4 catches for 68 yards and another touchdown.

What else is Jeremiah Smith supposed to do at this point? Even in last year’s playoff loss to the Miami Hurricanes he posted 157 yards and a touchdown. Against Oregon, he went nearly two full quarters without being targeted while the game got away from Ohio State. He can’t call the plays, throw, and catch.

There’s a lot of things that you can point to as going wrong in the Ohio State season, but Jeremiah Smith showing up in big games and continually proving himself to be one of the greatest receivers in the history of college football isn’t one of them.

KBO’s SSG Landers Sign Lyon Richardson
content:
The SSG Landers of the KBO League announced Thursday that right-hander Lyon Richardson was signed to a one-year deal.  Richardson will earn $900K in salary, plus he received a $100K signing bonus for putting pen to paper.

A second-round pick for the Reds in the 2018 draft, Richardson has appeared in parts of the last four MLB seasons, though the large majority of his big league work came in 2025.  Richardson has a 6.48 ERA, 17.2% strikeout rate, and 14.6% walk rate over 58 1/3 innings and 42 games in the Show, with 37 2/3 of those innings coming in 34 appearances with the 2025 Reds.

Cincinnati designated Richardson for assignment last offseason and then outrighted him off its 40-man roster, but selected Richardson again in May for what proved to be his final two MLB games with the Reds.  Richardson was then DFA’ed and outrighted again, and he opted for free agency and landed with the Brewers on a minor league deal.  This new beginning led to another DFA/outright cycle and a second minors contract with Milwaukee, and Richardson’s time in the organization resulted in 1 2/3 innings of big league work in one game.

Richardson is out of minor league options, and would’ve been limited to fielding only minors contracts this winter if he’d stayed focused on remaining in North America.  With the lockout looming, Richardson might not have found a new deal with an MLB team for months, so signing with the Landers gives him both added financial security and the ability to now focus solely on baseball.

While he has worked mostly as a reliever in the majors and minors over the last few years, Richardson will return to starting duties with the Landers.  Richardson’s career-long control problems remain an obstacle, but a solid showing in the KBO League could get him back onto the radar for MLB teams in a year’s time, and perhaps with a larger payday awaiting if he can re-establish his value as a starting pitcher.

Blue Jays Interested In Teruaki Sato
content:
At least seven teams have been publicly linked to Teruaki Sato’s market, and The Athletic’s Mitch Bannon reports that the Blue Jays also have interest in the Hanshin Tigers slugger.  The news comes as no surprise, given the Jays’ need for offense, their tendency to check in on virtually every free agent available, and the team’s increasing forays into the Japanese talent market.

Last winter’s signing of Kazuma Okamoto represents the high point of Toronto’s overtures to Japanese players, though Okamoto’s presence also creates a bit of an obstacle in regards to Sato, who is also a third baseman.  Sato also has experience as a corner outfielder and isn’t considered a premium defender at any of his positions, so he might well end up getting a good chunk of DH time in the majors.  The Blue Jays have vacancies to fill in both left field and DH, plus Sato could still get the odd turn at third base if Okamoto is given a DH day or an off-day.

Sato has been at least a productive hitter during all six of his NPB seasons, but his last two seasons in particular have been stellar, highlighted by a Triple Crown-winning campaign in 2026.  Sato delivered 39 homers, 106 RBI, and a .306/.383/.609 slash line over 614 PA for the Tigers last season, and he also went deep 40 times for the 2025 club.  If Sato can translate any of this power over to the majors, it would be a huge boost to a Blue Jays team that finished with a league-worst 152 home runs in 2026.

Despite all their offensive struggles last year, the Jays’ 19% strikeout rate was the second-lowest in baseball, topped only by the Rays.  Toronto has prioritized contact hitting and putting the ball in play, so this might make Sato less of a fit given how his NPB production has come along with a lot of strikeouts.  As Bannon notes, the Jays liked Okamoto last winter in part because he was known as a quality contact hitter in Japan, but Okamoto’s strikeout rate ballooned to 28.8% in his first year of MLB action.  In context, Sato had a 26.7 K% with the Tigers last year.

MLB Trade Rumors ranked Sato seventh on our list of the offseason’s top 50 free agents, and projected a five-year, $80MM deal for a player entering his age-28 season.  The price tag shouldn’t be much of an object for a Jays team that has paid the luxury tax in three of the last four seasons, and exceeded the maximum tax threshold in 2026.  The question is whether or not the Blue Jays would prefer to make another significant investment in a player without any MLB experience, or if the Jays would prefer to spend on a player with more of a proven track record.

Sato is one of many hitters reportedly on Toronto’s offseason radar thus far, as the team could feasibly look to address any position in the lineup except third base (Okamoto), starting catcher (Alejandro Kirk), and first base (Vladimir Guerrero Jr., coming off the worst season of his career).  Since pitching is also a need, the Blue Jays will surely want to check at least a couple of boxes off their lengthy offseason to-do list before the lockout.

title: Donte Whitner disgusted by Jameis Winston’s ‘Who Let The Dogs Out’ hard count
content:
Jameis Winston is a professional content creator despite his title of New York Giants backup quarterback. Some people can’t get enough of his cartoonish persona, while others see right through it.

Former NFL defensive back Donte Whitner has announced himself as a member of the latter group.

On Thursday night, the Giants lost a 24-21 heartbreaker to the visiting Washington Commanders. Late in the fourth quarter, Giants head coach John Harbaugh trotted out Winston to try to draw the Commanders offside on a fourth-and-1.

The Prime Video broadcast picked up Winston’s obnoxious cadence.

“Get ready! Get set! Hut 1, hut 2, hut 3!”

Alright, that’s performative, but not particularly memorable.

But then Winston started singing the 2000 Baha Men hit “Who Let The Dogs Out.”

If you listen to nothing else today, at least listen to Jameis Winston’s hard count here lmao https://t.co/F1nr26EN3W

— NFL (@NFL) November 13, 2026

Plenty of people thought it was hilarious, including Prime’s Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit, but Whitner didn’t crack a smile.

“I’d cut Jameis Winston this morning,” Whitner said on ESPN’s Get Up on Friday. “It was so unrealistic. You have 10 other guys other there, and guys on defense, busting their butt every week, and it’s very hard and difficult to win a game in the National Football League. So when you get up there—first and foremost, who ever says hut 1, hut 2, hut 3? That’s 1950s football!”

“And then when you go into ‘Who Let The Dogs Out’? Are you serious?” Whitner continued. “He’s clearly just trying to go viral on social media while they’re trying to win a football game. He’d get his pink slip this morning.”

Harry Douglas admitted to “crying laughing” in disbelief while watching Winston’s antics in his hotel room before Get Up host Mike Greenberg recentered the conversation on Whitner’s critique. Greenberg asked Douglas to weigh in on Winston seemingly “not taking seriously trying to get the other team to jump.”

“If anybody for the Washington Commanders would have jumped on ‘Who Let The Dogs Out’? If I’m [Washington head coach] Dan Quinn, I’m cutting their a**,” Douglas said.

Greenberg disclosed that everyone at Get Up laughed about it in the production meeting, except for Whitner. “I didn’t find it funny,” Whitner confirmed.

On Friday, reporters asked Harbaugh whether Winston’s colorful cadence bothered him.

“That ‘Who Let The Dogs Out’ thing, while it was, I think, probably fun on his part, so to speak, the way the cadence sounds, it was still an attempt to still draw them offsides,” Harbaugh said, per SNY.

“Does it bother me? No,” Harbaugh added. “I heard him do it in practice.”

The Giants briefly turned to Winston after Jaxson Dart underwent season-ending knee surgery in September. Winston’s short-lived stint as starting quarterback ended in Week 7, when the Giants opted for J.J. McCarthy. New York acquired McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 28.

The Giants (5-3-1) will next host the Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) at MetLife Stadium on Nov. 22.
