title: The Opener: Bauers, Ausmus, Kopech
content:
Former Padres owner Peter Seidler passed away at age 63 on this day in 2023.  Seidler was part of the Ron Fowler-led ownership group that bought the Padres in 2012, and then became club chairman in 2020 after buying out enough of Fowler’s stake of the team to become the majority shareholder.  In his three years of running the team, Seidler turned the Padres into one of the league’s biggest spenders in an all-out push to try and bring San Diego its first World Series title.  While the Padres only made it as far as the 2022 NLCS during Seidler’s brief tenure, Seidler became a beloved figure in baseball, and his legacy has carried forward as the team has remained in contention.

1. Bauers heads to Boston

The Red Sox made an early and somewhat unexpected splash in the free agent market yesterday, agreeing with Jake Bauers on a four-year, $58MM deal.  The plan is to have Bauers share the first base and DH duties with Willson Contreras, and with the designated hitter spot now essentially covered on a daily basis, it only increases the likelihood that odd men out Masataka Yoshida and Jarren Duran might not be back with the Sox in 2027.  With the November 20th non-tender deadline looming, Duran could simply be let go, given his projected $11.1MM salary.  Of the eight free agents who were issued qualifying offers, Bauers was perhaps the best candidate to accept the one-year, $23.15MM contract, so it seems likely that we won’t see anyone accepting the QO before Tuesday’s deadline.

2. Bagwell discusses Ausmus hiring

The Astros hired Brad Ausmus as their new manager earlier this week, and team senior advisor Jeff Bagwell provided some context on the decision in an interview with MLB.com’s Brian McTaggart.  Bagwell pointed to Ausmus’ varied resume on and off the field, and Ausmus’ experience as a catcher was of particular note.  “When you’re a catcher, you control so much with your team because you control your pitching staff,” Bagwell said.  “You cannot win without pitching.  We, for the last few years, have really worn our bullpen down and have gotten a lot of injuries.  I’m not saying it’s because of our coaching staff, but we have to have somebody that understands pitchers, and nobody does that better than catchers.”  While Ausmus and Bagwell are longtime friends dating back to their time as teammates in Houston, Bagwell dismissed the idea that he was “banging the table for Brad,” saying that owner Jim Crane and GM Randy Flores had to approve the hiring.  “Most people who get jobs in the game are friends with somebody.  That’s how it works.  How do you think you find people?  They just don’t show up.  You’ve got to find people, and generally, they’re acquaintances you have throughout the game,” Bagwell said.

3. Kopech set for showcase

Michael Kopech didn’t pitch in 2026, but the right-hander will throw for evaluators from multiple teams today, as reported by The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal, Will Sammon, and Katie Woo earlier this week.  A veteran of six MLB seasons, Kopech has found success as both a starter and a reliever, but was used only out of the bullpen in 2024-25 in the wake of a rough season in the White Sox rotation in 2023.  Injuries have been a major subplot of Kopech’s career, and shoulder and knee problems limited him to just 11 relief innings for the Dodgers in 2025.  The Giants and Yankees were linked to Kopech’s market last winter, but no deal was reached.  Kopech figures to have to settle for a minor league pact this winter, and if has solved his control problems and can stay healthy, he could offer plenty of upside to a team’s bullpen.

title: Oklahoma AD blasts decision to move Ole Miss game to Sunday after nationwide flight chaos
content:
The nationwide grounding of flights due to technical issues with flight control equipment has wrecked havoc on the Saturday slate of college football action with the game between Oklahoma and Ole Miss facing the biggest impact.

The contest between the Sooners and Rebels was originally scheduled for 4:15 p.m. ET on Saturday in Norman, Oklahoma. However, with the chaos affecting teams and programs all around the country, Ole Miss decided they couldn’t make trip in time.

The game has now been moved to Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in a rare instance of a major college football game being played on a day usually reserved for the NFL. And it appears that not all sides were supportive of the move.

Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny released a blistering statement that shaded Ole Miss for not being able to make the trip in spite of every other program in the country being able to make their destinations for Saturday games. He also said that the SEC forced the game to be played on Sunday, and if the Sooners denied, they would have to forfeit the contest.

https://t.co/6z039iPC1m

— Roger Denny (@Oklahoma_AD) November 14, 2026

Denny’s statement reads in full:

We recognize the extraordinary circumstances surrounding the ground stoppage and understand the challenges it created for teams across the country. As soon as we learned of Ole Miss’ travel issues, we immediately began communicating with their staff and our conference leadership. We were told that Ole Miss explored every avenue to travel to Norman and play on Saturday as planned. But, unlike every other team traveling for competition tomorrow, they were unable to find a solution. After multiple conversations with the league office, Commissioner Sankey informed us of his decision to move our game to Sunday, over our strong objection. After continued discussions, he further informed us that our failure to play on Sunday at the directed time would result in a forfeit.

Rescheduling the game has a significant impact, particularly on our fans. Those who have made travel arrangements, accommodations, and personal plans around a Saturday game now face unnecessary disruption and hardship. Their time, commitment, and investment deserve greater consideration than they were afforded in the conference’s decision tonight.

I understand that difficult decisions sometimes must be made under extraordinary circumstances. But those decisions must also consider the impact on everyone involved. Put simply, this decision isn’t fair to our athletes, our institution, or to Sooner Nation. But we’ve been given no other choice. We are obligated to play the game when directed, but we remain steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening.

We will continue to fight in the best interests of OU Athletics and always on behalf of our student-athletes and fans.

On Saturday, we will share more on game logistics and fan appreciation measures.

The move from Saturday to Sunday represents a whole bunch of logistical issues for Oklahoma as the host of the contest. Who knows how many fans will be affected and not be able to make the game on Sunday. And as ESPN star and Bussin’ with the Boys host Will Compton said, Ole Miss could have taken a long bus ride if they really wanted to make it to play on Saturday.

Ole Miss not hitting an 8-hour bus ride will sadly go down as the softest move in the 2026 college football season

A lot of “anywhere, anytime” speeches happening right now…

Not at Ole Miss

They’re not football guys

Sad

— Will Compton (@_willcompton) November 14, 2026

Could Ole Miss have made it to Norman in time if they really wanted to? The Sooners and their fans will definitely feel aggrieved to see their game delayed an entire day instead of a few hours. For college football fans nationwide, it provides a unique standalone game on Sunday if they want to take a break from the NFL. And given the statement from Oklahoma, there may be a little extra spice for this one.

title: Nick Saban couldn’t care less about ‘bullsh*t’ College Football Playoff rankings
content:
Nick Saban has openly opposed the newly legitimized expanded 24-team College Football Playoff on more than one occasion, and he isn’t particularly fond of the College Football Playoff rankings, either.

On Friday’s Pat McAfee Show, the legendary Alabama head football coach let it rip when Pat McAfee asked him to weigh in on this week’s rankings.

“To be honest with you, I think, at this point, the rankings are a little bit bullsh*t, if you want to know the truth about it,” Saban said. “I think there’s so many games to play and so many scenarios and all that. Who wins what is going to determine—like, UCLA being No. 4 doesn’t mean nothing if they can win out and beat USC. USC being 20th doesn’t mean anything if they beat Indiana and go beat UCLA.”

“As you see people move up and down based on wins and losses—I mean, Indiana didn’t even play, and they dropped, what? Five spots or something,” Saban added. “I’m like, how does that happen? But it happens. If they win this week, they’ll be right back in the mix of things.”

Saban is far from the first or last person to disparage the College Football Playoff rankings.

title: Red Sox To Sign Jake Bauers
content:
The Red Sox and first baseman Jake Bauers are in agreement on a four-year, $58MM contract, reports ESPN’s Jeff Passan. The VC Sports Group client received a $23.15MM qualifying offer from the Brewers but will turn that down and head to Boston on a lucrative multi-year contract.

Due in no small part to his postseason heroics, Bauers’ story is well known by now. The 31-year-old former top prospect was on the cusp of retirement after seemingly flaming out in the majors. He’d called his agent and informed him of the decision but changed course just days later when his wife learned she was pregnant with their second child and wouldn’t be going back to work — and securing health insurance — as they’d planned. Bauers signed back with the Brewers on a minor league deal ahead of the 2025 season and made the club. Bauers struggled for much of the season and looked like a DFA or non-tender candidate until a massive September saved his roster spot.

That September surge proved to be a portent for a full-fledged breakout. Bauers wasn’t just the Brewers’ best hitter and the eventual NLCS MVP in 2026 — he was one of the best hitters in the entire sport. Dating back to early September of 2025, Bauers has taken 631 regular season plate appearances and mashed at a .276/.396/.494 pace with 28 homers and a 16% walk rate. His 26.1% strikeout rate is too high, but for a player with this type of patience and power output, that’s a more than worthwhile trade-off.

By measure of wRC+, Bauers has been 48% better than average at the plate since September of 2025. Newly minted American League MVP Yordan Alvarez and Yankees star Ben Rice are the only two hitters with a better wRC+ than Bauers in that time. His 148 wRC+ places him in a four-way tie with Juan Soto, Shohei Ohtani and newly crowned NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong for the game’s third-best mark.

Bauers has averaged a whopping 92.1 mph off the bat with a huge 14% barrel rate and 51.9% hard-hit rate throughout his breakout, and his renaissance hasn’t been the product of selective matchups. While Bauers struggled against lefties for the majority of his career, he’s been platoon-proof throughout this turnaround, crushing lefties at a .267/.375/.526 pace with a 14.4% walk rate and 23% strikeout rate in 160 plate appearances.

Even if Bauers can’t sustain this level of nearly superhuman performance, there’s good reason to buy into him as a bona fide middle-of-the-order hitter now. In 2026, Statcast placed him in the top 10% of big league hitters in terms of average exit velocity, hard-hit rate, barrel rate, bat speed and expected wOBA. He was tied for the fourth-highest walk rate in baseball, and only 11 qualified hitters chased pitches off the plate at a lower rate than Bauers’ 21.7%.

Bauers had already hit his way into becoming a prominent piece of the Brewers’ lineup by the time the playoffs rolled around, but he thrust himself into the national spotlight with a monster NLCS performance against the Dodgers. Bauers flummoxed Yoshinobu Yamamoto with a marathon, 12-pitch at-bat that culminated in a walk, helping elevate the L.A. ace’s pitch count and chase him from the game in the third inning. He embarked on an 11-pitch battle against two-time Cy Young winning lefty Blake Snell the following night and did one better — belting a go-ahead two-run homer that played a pivotal role in Milwaukee’s sweep of the Dodgers. Bauers went 4-for-14 with that homer, a double and three walks en route to NLCS MVP honors.

The Red Sox are a surprising fit from a roster perspective, but they’re clearly prioritizing Bauers’ breakout production and sorting out the positional fit later. Willson Contreras played a fine first base in Boston last year, and the outfield — where Bauers is a stretch defensively anyhow — is already crowded. Ceddanne Rafaela is locked into center field, with Wilyer Abreu, Jarren Duran, Roman Anthony and Masataka Yoshida all in the mix for corner outfield/designated hitter time. Former first baseman Triston Casas, out since early 2025 with a major knee injury, is also still on the roster.

Boston is known to be shopping Duran, and Yoshida is a trade or release candidate himself as he enters the final season of a five-year deal that hasn’t gone to plan. Casas, like Duran, is a change of scenery candidate but also has minor league options remaining. If the Sox plan to move on from the Duran/Yoshida/Casas trio (or enter 2027 with Casas in the minors), they could go with Anthony, Rafaela and Abreu in the outfield, Contreras at first base, and Bauers as the primary designated hitter (with occasional reps at first base and in left field).

As MLBTR’s Payroll Tracker shows, Boston was projected for a bit more than $208MM prior to signing Bauers. We don’t know what next year’s luxury tax thresholds will be — or if the system will even be in place — but the Sox were already north of 2026’s $244MM CBT threshold. Bauers’ contract will add another $14.5MM annually to their tax considerations. The 2027 season would be their third consecutive year as tax payors, so they’d pay a 50% tax on the first $20MM by which they exceed the theoretical threshold, a 62% tax on the next $20MM, a 95% tax on the next $20MM and a 110% tax on anything beyond that point.

Because the Sox were tax payors for the 2026 season, they’ll have to forfeit their second- and fifth-highest draft selections in order to sign Bauers, who rejected his qualifying offer with the Brewers. Boston will also see next offseason’s bonus pool for signing international amateurs reduced by $1MM. The Brewers, meanwhile, will receive a compensatory pick for losing a free agent who’d been given a qualifying offer. Had Bauers signed for under $50MM, that pick would’ve come after Competitive Balance Round B — around No. 75 in the draft. Since he signed for more than $50MM, the pick will instead come at the end of the first round.

title: Giants Notes: Rotation, Bullpen, Catcher
content:
The Giants have made no secret of their desire to add at least one starter. They’re not planning to make a run at Tarik Skubal and seem to be out on Trevor Rogers, who’s attached to draft compensation via the qualifying offer. San Francisco has been loosely linked to Freddy Peralta and to NPB righty Kaima Taira, though there’s a decent chance they look more to the middle tiers of the market.

Logan Webb and Landen Roupp are the only two starters locked into the season-opening rotation. President of baseball operations Buster Posey has implicitly suggested that next season might be something of a bridge year with most of their top prospect talent in the lower minors. However, USA Today’s Bob Nightengale writes that they’re continuing to rebuff teams who call about Webb.

That’s not surprising, as the Giants publicly shot down speculation about trading their ace early in deadline season. Webb is signed for two more seasons. There’s a reasonable argument for listening on him if the Giants aren’t going to make an all-in push next year, but the organization clearly doesn’t want to embark on a full rebuild either. If they were going to listen on Webb, it’d have made more sense to do it over the summer when they were en route to a 97-loss season.

That leaves three spots up for grabs. Adrian Houser seems to have the leg up on one of those. Posey told Alex Pavlovic on the Giants Talk podcast that he “views Houser in the rotation,” though that came with a caveat the team was likely to deploy the opener more frequently. That’s not going to be unique to Houser, but he’ll be a frequent candidate as the team tries to navigate his deficiencies against left-handed hitters.

Houser’s sinker-heavy arsenal has been more effective against right-handed batters throughout his career. That was particularly true this year, as lefties teed off at a .282/.367/.516 clip with 12 homers in 284 plate appearances. Right-handed hitters mustered only a .222/.234/.318 mark across 186 trips. Houser would ideally be in a swing or pure relief role, but the Giants are paying him $13.5MM for the second season of his surprise $22MM contract. They also simply don’t have many alternatives in the starting staff with Hayden Birdsong, Blade Tidwell, Carson Whisenhunt and Trevor McDonald all set to miss part or all of the season recovering from Tommy John surgeries.

San Francisco is sure to bring in at least one starter and could leave an open competition among the likes of Anthony Molina, Matt Wilkinson, Yunior Marte and Cesar Perdomo for a spot. They’re also going to need to do a lot of work in the bullpen. That’s true at the back end, where Posey said they’re in the closing market. It also applies to the middle relief group — especially if they’re going to more aggressively play matchups to try to compensate for the lack of rotation depth.

Alex Pavlovic of NBC Sports Area and Shayna Rubin of The San Francisco Chronicle each wrote this week that the Giants are likely to bring in a left-handed reliever. They traded Erik Miller at the deadline and moved on from both Matt Gage and Reiver Sanmartin at season’s end. Sam Hentges is their only returning lefty reliever; he walked almost 15% of opponents in his first year back from shoulder surgery.

It’s a reasonably deep class of lefties on the free agent market. The Giants are highly unlikely to give up draft capital for Adrian Morejon and might be priced out on Alex Vesia and Gregory Soto. They could still look to old friend Steven Okert, Sean Newcomb, Brock Burke or A.J. Minter as borderline two-year deal candidates. José Alvarado and A.J. Puk are reclamation upside fliers, while Tim Hill and Hoby Milner are available as low-slot matchup specialists. Jon Heyman of The New York Post reported this week that the Giants were among the teams with interest in Hill, who led MLB with a 69% ground-ball rate for the Yankees this year.

While pitching is the front office’s focus, it’s possible they make a move behind the plate as well. Posey told Pavlovic on Giants Talk that bringing in a veteran catcher is “something we have to look at.” They traded Patrick Bailey in May and relied on three rookies — Daniel Susac, Drew Cavanaugh and Jesus Rodriguez — for a good chunk of the summer. Susac and Rodriguez each missed the final seven weeks of the season to injury, leading to Cavanaugh getting the bulk of the playing time down the stretch. They brought in journeyman Andrew Knizner as a stopgap backup but dropped him from the 40-man roster a couple weeks ago.

“We’re very excited about Susac, Cavanuagh and J-Rod, even (Adrián Sugastey) in Triple-A,” Posey told Pavlovic. “But they’re all young. It’s something we’ve talked about as a group. … It’s helpful for a young catcher to have a guy that’s done it for a while.” Veteran backup types available in free agency include Austin Hedges, James McCann, Christian Vázquez and Kyle Higashioka.

title: Rays Rumors: DeLuca, McClanahan, Pepiot, Rasmussen
content:
The Rays could make center fielder Jonny DeLuca available in trade this offseason, write Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic. The idea would be to open center field for Victor Mesa Jr., who played mostly right field this year.

DeLuca is coming off a career-best year in his third season as a Ray. He stole 17 bases and connected 11 home runs while batting .266/.300/.429 in a career-high 370 plate appearances. He divided his defensive workload between center and right field, playing strong defense at both spots. The 28-year-old missed a month with a right hamstring strain but was on the field much more often than he had been in 2025. The Oregon product was limited to 20 games that year by a right shoulder strain and a left hamstring injury.

The righty-hitting DeLuca provides most of his value in a speed and defense capacity. He’s a serviceable but unexceptional hitter, batting .250/.295/.389 in his career. DeLuca has had reverse platoon splits, posting a .709 OPS against righties compared to a .642 mark versus left-handed pitching. He has an aggressive approach and doesn’t make a ton of hard contact. He’s an elite runner who rates as one of the rangiest defensive outfielders in the game. DeLuca is under arbitration control for three seasons and projected by MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz for a $1.7MM salary.

Although Mesa isn’t quite as fast, he played very strong defense in a little over 500 right field innings. Mesa batted .260/.327/.498 with 14 home runs across 262 plate appearances, emerging as a key contributor after being acquired from Miami in a DFA trade. If the Rays were to play him more frequently in center field, they could look for a corner bat via free agency or trade. Ryan Vilade, Jacob Melton and Jack Suwinski are all on the 40-man roster. Top center field prospect Theo Gillen could open the season in Triple-A and might make his debut by the second half of 2027.

The Rays frequently deal role players as they get into their arbitration windows. There are a few similar possibilities on the pitching staff, as Rosenthal and Sammon suggest that starters Shane McClanahan and Ryan Pepiot could also be available. Although The Athletic report doesn’t mention Griffin Jax, one imagines the Rays will receive calls on him as well.

McClanahan and Jax are both entering their final arbitration years, respectively projected for $6.6MM and $5.7MM salaries. Pepiot is projected at $3.1MM and under club control for two seasons. All three pitchers are currently slated to be in Kevin Cash’s rotation, yet the Rays will surely be on the lookout for arms with more extended team control windows.

Pepiot, who was acquired alongside DeLuca in the 2023 Tyler Glasnow trade, missed all of 2026 recovering from right hip surgery. He pitched at a mid-rotation level before the injury, making 31 starts with a 3.67 ERA while striking out a quarter of opponents last year. President of baseball operations Erik Neander said last week that he’s expected to be full go for Spring Training.

McClanahan is a former ace who has struggled to stay healthy since undergoing elbow surgery three years ago. The 29-year-old southpaw remains effective when healthy, pitching to a 3.36 ERA with a league average strikeout and walk profile across 24 starts this past season. He had two injured list stints and missed the playoff run due to forearm tightness. He’s also expected to have a normal offseason.

Jax was the latest midseason bullpen to starter move for a Tampa Bay team that has had a lot of success in that regard. He worked 112 1/3 frames of 3.53 ERA ball and fanned a quarter of opposing hitters. He has plenty of experience at the back of the bullpen but looks like a capable mid-rotation starter. Tampa Bay will probably be in the rotation market even if they don’t move any of McClanahan, Jax or Pepiot. They’d certainly need to backfill at least one spot if they trade a starter. They’re already losing Nick Martinez and Freddy Peralta to free agency.

Drew Rasmussen is slated to anchor the group. He’s coming off his second straight top 10 Cy Young finish and has stayed healthy for the last two seasons. The Rays exercised a $20MM option on Rasmussen for 2027, the final year of his contract. Neander began the offseason by saying they currently intend to hang onto their ace, who’d make the highest salary in team history.

Assuming that’s the case, the likeliest outcome is that Rasmussen would depart next offseason in free agency. The Rays would presumably receive some kind of compensation, either through the qualifying offer or something similar in the next collective bargaining agreement. However, Neander implied to FanSided’s Robert Murray at the GM Meetings that the Rays would have some interest in extension talks.

Rasmussen is currently slated to hit free agency in his age-32 season. If he stays healthy next year, he could command a three- or four-year deal at $25-30MM annually. That’s not traditionally a Rays move, though they did sign Glasnow to an extension that had a $25MM salary in the final season. (They traded him to the Dodgers before that year.) They don’t have any guaranteed contracts beyond next year and have forecasted a future payroll uptick with the expectation they’ll have a new stadium in the City of Tampa for the 2029 season.

title: ABC and ESPN address concerns over nationwide ground stop delaying college football games
content:
By Friday night, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted a nationwide ground stop, which lasted nearly four hours. According to HuffPost, the ground stop delayed nearly 10,000 flights and led to the cancellation of 5,000 flights, so the chaotic aftermath is just getting started.

The ripple effect could disturb the weekend’s sports slate, particularly college football games, but ABC and ESPN jointly assured fans on the games under their purview.

“Source says ESPN/ABC is prepared to produce all the college football games on their schedule tomorrow and still working out specific details,” Richard Deitsch reported. “Think others have noted this, but Kirk Herbstreit is in Boise for College GameDay and assigned to Texas-LSU.

“So his travel would clearly be TBD right now, but ESPN (as other networks do) will have announcers in place to work that game if needed. I don’t know who would fill in for Herbstreit. Big picture: Wishing everyone who has been impacted by this all the best and obviously the safest of journeys ahead.”

All college football games set to broadcast across ABC and ESPN on Saturday can be found in Awful Announcing’s trusty Week 11 college football announcing schedule.

Shortly after the ground stop went into effect, ESPN’s Pete Thamel reported at least 13 college football teams’ flights were “in limbo”:

title: Nationals Release Kyle Nicolas
content:
The Nationals released reliever Kyle Nicolas, according to the MLB.com transaction tracker. Washington designated him for assignment a week ago when they acquired Reiver Sanmartin from San Francisco.

Nicolas never pitched in a major league game with the Nats. Washington acquired the righty from the Orioles in early July, a trade most notable for being the first between the franchises after two decades of acrimony. They kept him on optional assignment to Triple-A Rochester for the rest of the season. Nicolas turned in a 3.27 ERA with a 29% strikeout rate for the Red Wings, but he walked a massive 18.7% of batters faced. Washington didn’t give him a look despite having one of the worst bullpens in the league.

A former Competitive Balance Round draftee out of Ball State, Nicolas has pitched parts of four MLB seasons between the Pirates and Reds. He’s posted an earned run average just under 5.00 across 105 1/3 career innings. Nicolas has huge stuff, sitting in the 98-99 mph range and sporting both a power slider and curveball. He’s never been able to harness it effectively, walking 14% of MLB opponents and more than 16% of batters faced at the Triple-A level.

Nicolas has never been outrighted in his career. Washington could have kept him in the farm system without a roster spot but elected to release him. That sometimes indicates a player is weighing overseas interest.

title: Royals In Market For Right-Handed Hitting Outfielder
content:
The Royals are looking for a right-handed hitting outfielder, general manager J.J. Picollo told reporters at the GM Meetings this week (link via ESPN’s Jesse Rogers). The GM added that an acquisition would ideally be capable of playing center field on at least a part-time basis.

That’s essentially the role Lane Thomas played for K.C. this year. They picked him up on a one-year, $5.25MM free agent contract last offseason. Thomas played reasonably well for a half-season, batting .232/.326/.393 across 97 games. He started 72 contests in the outfield, 52 of them up the middle. They traded him to Atlanta at the deadline for a pair of minor league pitchers and to dump what remained of Bailey Falter’s arbitration salary.

Thomas didn’t play particularly well for the Braves. He’s back on the market and might be available even more cheaply than he was a year ago if the Royals wanted to reengage. Tyrone Taylor, Myles Straw, Jake Meyers and Victor Robles are other possibilities as fourth/fifth outfield types. If the Royals wanted a potential everyday center fielder, Luis Robert Jr. is the top right-handed hitter on the free agent market.

Dane Myers and Jonny DeLuca are fourth outfielders who could be available on the trade front. The Nationals are fielding interest in former second overall pick Dylan Crews, who’s a change of scenery candidate. Washington will probably be looking for an affordable pitcher in return, though, and that’s not an area of organizational strength for Kansas City. The Royals might balk at giving up Noah Cameron given Crews’ lack of big league production to this point. Players like Luinder Avila (who’ll likely miss next season after August Tommy John surgery) or Daniel Lynch IV don’t seem enticing enough for Washington to part with a player who has Crews’ draft and prospect pedigree.

Kansas City arguably should be looking for two outfield acquisitions. Right fielder Jac Caglianone is their only clear regular. Left fielder Isaac Collins underwhelmed in his first season after being acquired from Milwaukee. Kyle Isbel is a strong defensive center fielder but had a career-worst .224/.268/.323 showing at the plate. He’s in his final year of arbitration control and a potential non-tender candidate on a projected $3.5MM salary (courtesy of MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz). Even if the Royals keep Isbel around, they’d ideally push him into a true fourth outfield role. Tyler Tolbert and John Rave are fifth outfield types.

There’s room on the roster for K.C. to both add a right-handed hitting center fielder like Taylor or Meyers and acquire a true everyday player in left field. Ian Happ, Taylor Ward, Ramón Laureano, and Trent Grisham are free agent possibilities. Former K.C. target Jarren Duran is all but guaranteed to be traded or non-tendered by the Red Sox after they agreed to a four-year deal with Jake Bauers. Brandon Marsh and JJ Bleday are other trade possibilities.

On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) declared a nationwide ground stop. The only other nationwide ground stops in recent U.S. history came on Sept. 11, 2001 and in January 2023.

As of this writing, The New York Times is reporting more than 3,000 canceled flights, and CNN reported that government officials have “no timetable for resolution.”

Olivia Rinaldi of CBS News reported that “an update to the private communications network” connecting the country’s air traffic control system “caused the system to reboot,” and the reboot triggered a crash.

title: Mauricio Pochettino Leaves The USMNT For An Even Bigger Mess
content:
After an extended denouement to a doomed tenure, Manchester United finally set manager Michael Carrick loose on Thursday, hoping to put an end to the club's worst league start in 40 years. On Friday, the next era for England's most famous club began, sort of, as United announced that Mauricio Pochettino would be leaving the U.S. men's national team on Nov. 18 in order to become the new boss at Old Trafford.

Carrick's departure is no surprise, but Pochettino's arrival counts as a bit of a shock. Pochettino had famously come to international prominence first at Southampton and then in his five-season-plus stint at Tottenham Hotspur, which saw that club's evolution from an also-ran into, well, an also-ran that could actually fight with the big boys. Eventually, his tenure there grew stale and the lack of trophies forced a move, with Tottenham firing him in November of 2019. The Argentine then took a year off before signing on to succeed Thomas Tuchel at Paris Saint-Germain in early 2021; his first half-season there wasn't great, as he oversaw the only PSG squad to not win the Ligue 1 title this decade. He did go on to win the league in his first full season, but PSG let him go in the summer of 2022 anyway. A return to the Premier League with Chelsea followed in 2023, where he finished in sixth place in his only season at Stamford Bridge.

That brings us to September 2024, when Pochettino became manager of the USMNT ahead of the 2026 World Cup cycle. His appointment was a big deal, as he became the highest-paid and most accomplished manager in the country's history (Jurgen Klinsmann will quibble with the latter assessment, but whatever) in advance of a home(-ish) World Cup. Pochettino had a rocky start there, but eventually righted the ship enough to guide the USMNT to a Group D first-place finish and a Round of 32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. An embarrassing loss to Belgium in the Round of 16 put a bit of a damper on the run, but overall, Pochettino did what he was hired to do: help the USMNT perform at the World Cup.

title: Would You Get Stoned With The Scythians?
content:
It's just like they told you it would happen in D.A.R.E.: You have been miraculously, tragically transported 2,800 years back in time, in the land that is now the Uyuk Valley of southern Siberia. The site will be eventually called Tunnug 1 by the archaeologists who excavate it in 2017. But that is the future, and this is the present, meaning 800 B.C. You have come to sit with the Scythians, nomads who roamed the Eurasian steppes on horseback. You have even glimpsed their warrior-king, whose long and stately braids make him seem like a pretty cool guy. Also, he's smoking. Suddenly the warrior-king glimpses you back, his reddish eyes glinting in the firelight. He leans over to you, whispers something inscrutable in an Eastern Iranic language, and extends in his grizzled hands an ancient joint, leaving you with only one question: Would you smoke that shit?

There are, to be certain, pros and cons. But one thing is clear, per a paper published recently in the journal Science: The Scythians were definitely using cannabis to get high. The analysis, led by Fabio-haired University of Bern archaeologist Gino Caspari, represents the earliest definitive evidence of humans consuming marijuana as a psychoactive drug, which was previously only traced back 2,500 years ago where Sogdian mourners once lit up in the ancient Jirzankal Cemetery in what is now western China.

It's only fitting that marijuana hails from one of the highest places in the world: the eastern Tibetan Plateau, also known as the Roof of the World. The plant evolved around 28 million years ago, and as early as 4,000 years ago Chinese farmers cultivated the plant for rope, clothing, and paper, per Science. But it is harder to tell when in the archaeological record ancient people first became gone off that loud. Wild weed, the ancestors of the domesticated kind, has only a little tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC, the plant's intoxicating compound. Some researchers confirmed this when they tried to smoke wild weed and felt nothing, also per Science. (It is unclear if these particular researchers are also the paper's authors, who described cannabis as an "illicit" substance.)

title: Horny Nvidia CEO No Longer CEO, Possibly Still Horny
content:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who is worth over $100 billion, resigned as CEO on Thursday morning, following an emergency board meeting prompted by several reports that he'd been having various affairs, most notably with someone U.S. officials believe was spying on behalf of the Chinese government.

Nvidia has an unorthodox corporate structure, built around Huang, which largely eschews traditional executive roles in favor of a large council of vice presidents who report directly to Huang, which makes the matter of his succession trickier to game out than it would be in other cases of a CEO doing sex stuff. He'll be succeeded on an interim basis by Colette Kress, formerly the CFO, whom Wired characterizes as one of the few people with a high-level grasp of the company's finances and ties to Wall Street.

A quick recap of how we got here: Nvidia is the single most important hardware technology company in the world, a chip designer that boosted its market cap to more than $4 trillion by making the must-have picks and shovels of the ongoing AI boom. As such, Nvidia is something like a shadow arm of the U.S. government, the latter of which is engaged in the stupidest-ever version of the space race with China over who can build the machine god first. Nvidia wants to sell its best stuff to Chinese companies because it doesn't really care who wins, as long as it makes money for investors, but the Trump administration won't allow it. Meanwhile, the tip-top Chinese AI companies have found ways to smuggle in the best Nvidia chips via third parties mostly based in Southeast Asia.

title: How I Succumbed To Reef Madness And Came To Love A Slowly Sinking Ship
content:
The SS United States finally sank in the Gulf of Mexico at around 10 p.m. ET Wedneday night. Not since the Minnow had a doomed vessel’s last tour run so far over schedule and still kept viewers engaged. Those who stuck with the 10-hour livestream were rewarded with an amazingly touching denouement. 

The ship had its day. The SS United States hit the seas in 1952, and at 990 feet long was about 100 feet longer than the Titanic, yet was able to hit speeds of more than 38 knots, still faster than any transatlantic ocean liner ever. But it was deemed obsolete and taken out of service way back in 1969, and spent the last 30 years docked in Philadelphia. Attempts to keep the SS US above water as a hotel or museum failed, and some folks in Okaloosa County, Florida, decided the liner was most valuable at the bottom of sea. The county floated a $10 million plan to turn the ship into an artificial reef and thereby enhance the Redneck Riviera’s reputation as a fishing and scuba diving destination. This entailed sinking the SS US about 22 miles off Fort Walton Beach during the very same week that the Edmund Fitzgerald hit bottom 51 years earlier.

title: ‘Mario Vargas Llosa: A Life’ Is Dishy And Definitive
content:
Mario Vargas Llosa: A Life might seem like a bland title for a biography, until it dawns on you exactly how much living the man did. He eloped with his aunt at 19, then humiliated her by writing a novel about it translated into more than 30 languages; divorced her for her much younger niece, his first cousin; and, after a scandalous 50-year marriage beset by separations, walked out one last time for the Spanish socialite and tabloid favorite Isabel Preysler, ex-wife of Julio Iglesias and mother of Enrique.

Arguably the world’s most famous Peruvian after Paddington, Vargas Llosa would have been president if not for the dark-horse populist Alberto Fujimori—father of the current president—who handily defeated Vargas Llosa’s platform of neoliberal shock economics in 1990. And in 2010, at age 74, he won the Nobel Prize in Literature, joining the pantheon alongside his lifelong frenemy Gabriel García Márquez, whom he famously punched in the face at a film premiere, for reasons that remain unclear. 

Thus, the page count of the new biography—the first since his death in 2025 and almost certainly the last word on the subject—clocking in at 812. Gerald Martin, a British critic who also wrote the definitive book on García Márquez, spent 25 years interviewing Vargas Llosa and those who knew him. The result is a monumental achievement: a synthesis of his subject's personal and political life with a surgical yet shockingly breezy analysis of the writing itself. And while it’s not always right to conflate fictional characters with their creator, Vargas Llosa is a special case, Martin argues: a novelist who peppered his work with confessions.

title: New York Knicks star OG Anunoby wins NBA championship in Skechers – a historic first
content:
History was made at the Frost Bank Center — and Skechers was right there on the court for every step of it.
OG Anunoby has been crowned an NBA Champion, becoming the first player in history to win an NBA title wearing Skechers Basketball footwear. For a brand that launched its basketball division just three years ago, it marks a defining moment.
Fresh off his iconic game-winning tip-in in Game 4, OG delivered another standout performance in the title-clinching Game 5, finishing with 28 points, five rebounds and two blocks while providing the two-way impact that helped power the Knicks to the championship.
From timely three-pointers to key defensive stops, Anunoby was one of the NBA Finals’ most influential performers throughout the series — and he did it all in Skechers. In true OG fashion, he even rotated through three pairs of Skechers during Game 5 alone: opening the game in a black colourway SKX Nexus, transitioning into the SKX Nexus “NYC Blue” PE, and closing out the championship in a yellow colourway SKX Nexus — a fitting exclamation point on a historic night.
        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by SKECHERS (@skechers)

Throughout the playoffs and Finals, OG captivated fans not only with his performances, but also with the Skechers Player Exclusive styles he wore on court — several of which went viral:
SKX Nexus “Euro” PE
This style led to a now-legendary exchange and gifting moment with Knicks fan and Skechers ambassador Martha Stewart.
SKX Reign “Foreman” PE
Debuted during warmups ahead of Game 3 of the Finals as a nod to his repeated Defensive Player of the Game honours.
SKX Nexus “NYC Blue” PE
This bold blue-and-orange colourway, worn during his iconic Game 4 performance, paid tribute to the Knicks’ remarkable playoff run and the fans who made it possible.
        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by SKECHERS (@skechers)

On court, OG rotated between two high-performance Skechers Basketball models that reflect his dynamic and versatile game:
• The SKX Nexus™ – a low-top performance shoe built for speed, stability and responsive comfort.
• The SKX Reign™ – designed for elevation and elite traction to keep OG locked in at both ends of the floor.
The milestone extends beyond basketball. OG is now a two-time NBA Champion, having first won a title with the Toronto Raptors in 2019, when he became the first British-born player to win an NBA championship.
Skechers is the world’s third-largest footwear brand and has rapidly assembled one of basketball’s most exciting athlete rosters, including Joel Embiid, Julius Randle, Isaiah Hartenstein, Norman Powell and WNBA stars Jackie Young, Rickea Jackson and Kiki Iriafen, alongside elite athletes across running, golf, football, pickleball and cricket.

title: SPIA celebrates the Middle East’s sports industry stars in gala evening in Abu Dhabi
content:
The 13th edition of the Sports Industry Awards (SPIA) returned to Abu Dhabi for a second successive year to celebrate the region’s finest in a special evening. 
Hosted by Sport36X and Interact as part of Sport Industry Series, Wednesday’s gala event at the Space42 Arena welcomed over 500 guests to the capital’s Space42 Arena to honour the individuals, organizations, venues and initiatives that are shaping the sports industry across the Middle East.
The awards night was held in a strategic partnership with the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi, with further support being extended by the Abu Dhabi Sports Council (ADSC). Jetour Elite Group Holding served as the Title Sponsor of the event, while Motus One came on board as the Gold Sponsor. MRamez Events and Spinneys were the Silver and Bronze sponsors respectively, with The Athletic making their debut as the media partners.
Winners across 26 different categories were selected by an independent panel of judges composed of industry stalwarts, chosen for their expertise in the Middle East sports industry. DP World Tour Championship, the 3rd Asian Youth Games Bahrain 2025, ADNOC Abu Dhabi Marathon and the ADEK All-Stars program were some of the big winners on the night.

The evening began with speeches from Bassam Nawfal, Managing Director of Sport360X and Sally Corander, Founder and CEO of Interact. H.E, Saeed Al Fazari, Strategic Affairs Executive Director of the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi then addressed the gathering to highlight the Emirate’s unwavering commitment to promote sport in the region.
“Over thirteen editions, SPIA has grown into far more than an awards ceremony. It has become the platform that brings this industry together. It recognises excellence. It sets the benchmark for what the very best looks like in sport across the Middle East,” Bassam said in his opening address.

“Earlier this year, our region went through a period that tested us. It affected all of us in different ways, and it reached every corner of our lives – our families, our communities and our industry. But, what stands out today is not the challenge. It is the response.

“The resilience of the UAE. Of Abu Dhabi. And, of the people in this room. Welcoming so many illustrious guests to Space42 Arena is a testament to the passion and momentum behind the Middle East’s sports industry.

“From outstanding campaigns to world-class facilities, the calibre of this year’s winners was truly inspiring. We’re also grateful to all our partners and sponsors whose support made this latest celebration possible.”
The different winners were selected after an extensive process of vetting more than hundred nominees by an esteemed panel of industry titans from across the region. 

These included: H.H. Princess Nouf Al Saud (General Manager – Marketing, Ministry of Sport Saudi Arabia), H.H. Ali Abdulrahman Al Ali (CEO, Dubai Racing Club), Richard Scudamore (Former Executive Chairman & CEO, Premier League), Fiona Jordan (Chief Brand Officer, Whisper), Mo Harb (Head of Partnerships, Tik Tok MENA), Melissa Moncada (CEO & Founder, Aurora Group), Danny Townsend (CEO, SURJ Sports Investment), Tom Foley (CEO, Go Sport), Shaima Alhusseini (Saudi Sports for all Federation, Managing Director), Sarah Swanson (Chief Brand Officer, WTA Ventures), Rob Pilgrim (Head of Sports EMEA, META), Jamie Dean (Executive Director – Sports, MODON), Simon Morris (Vice President, Marketing, International, Adobe), Karim Younes (Partner and COO, Entergame Sports Marketing), and Nick Pinder (Vice President of Sponsorships and Partnerships, International Cricket Council).

The DP World Tour Championship walked away with the coveted ‘Major Global Sports Event of the Year’ award while Elevate took home the ‘Best Agency of the Year’ trophy. The 3rd Asian Youth Games Bahrain 2025 clinched two awards on the night in the form of ‘Best Use of Social Media in Sport’ and ‘Athlete Wellbeing and Support Programme.’

The Yas Marina Circuit won the ‘Best Venue of the Year’ trophy while the ADNOC Abu Dhabi Marathon was the selection for ‘Best Fan Engagement in Sports.’ The ‘Amateur Sports Team/Club of the Year’ award was given to Banaat FC, while Desert Vipers were recognised for their ‘Excellence in Sustainability.’

The NBA Abu Dhabi games presented by ADQ won big by bagging the prestigious ‘Campaign of the Year’ award.

Two special recognition awards were also presented on the night. H.E. Ghanim Mubarak Al Hajeri was recognised as the ‘’Visionary Leader in Middle East Sport ’ while Cherie Pridham was presented with the ‘Female Leader in the Middle East’ recognition.

A highlight of the night was the interactive quiz of regional sports presented by Kahoot, with the attendees competing for lucrative prizes.

title: XX | HER EDITION launches women focused fitness competition as global events return to Dubai
content:
As the global events industry regains momentum following a period of uncertainty, a new fitness competition is launching in Dubai, one that shifts the focus away from elite performance and toward personal progress and participation.
XX | HER EDITION, a Dubai-born female fitness event, has been created specifically for women who are new to functional fitness or returning after time away. In an industry traditionally dominated by elite athletes and high-performance competition, XX is designed to make fitness more accessible, prioritising participation and community, while making competition more approachable.
Taking place on May 14, in partnership with GMG, the debut event will welcome 160 women to take part in a 30-minute functional fitness challenge completed in pairs. The format is designed to offer women the opportunity to experience the energy of competition in a uniquely supportive and inclusive environment.
The event brings together leading home-grown concepts and international brands from GMG’s portfolio – including Geant, Sun & Sand Sports and Supercare – alongside brands such as Built For Athletes and Science in Sport. All aligning with a shared vision to support women’s health, fitness, and wellbeing at a grassroots level. Hosting the event will be Rich Hayes, well-known podcast host and radio DJ, bringing his signature energy to the competition floor.
Behind XX | HER EDITION is Hannah Hall, CEO of Grassports and a seasoned event designer with over 16 years of experience delivering major sporting events across the UAE. Her portfolio includes industry-leading projects such as the DP World ILT20, Spinneys Dubai 92 Cycle Challenge, Arabian Warrior, and Women’s Epic Arabia.
Hannah Hall comments, “Sports and fitness events need a shake-up. There has been too much focus on elite performance for too long. XX | HER EDITION is about creating a platform for everyday women, those starting out, returning, or simply looking for a new challenge in a supportive environment. Participation should be celebrated just as much as performance.”
She continues,“We’re also seeing a shift in how brands want to engage with communities. Our partners understand that investing in real people, real journeys, and accessible fitness experiences has far greater long-term impact.”
Florian Hüthmair, President – Everyday Goods, said: “We aim to be an enabler for community events by bringing active living-inspired experiences to our customers. Through partnerships like XX | HER EDITION, we’re helping create welcoming spaces where women can show up, try something new, and feel supported—whether they’re just starting out or returning to fitness. Our objective is simple: to bring people together through movement and create environments where communities can connect, grow, and thrive.”
He continues: “At Géant we will continue to create in-store experiences for families and beyond, becoming the everyday premium food retail space where quality is daily and shopping is exciting.
“Our strategy revolves around food culture, music & art, and sports & active living. Our objective is to make Géant a true community hub—bringing people together through curated experiences, supporting healthier everyday choices, and creating a space where families and communities can connect, discover, and thrive.”
Following its launch, XX | HER EDITION will expand into a four-event series, including indoor summer editions and a trail-based event planned for winter 2026, continuing to grow its inclusive fitness community across the region.
With its focus on accessibility, empowerment, and community, XX | HER EDITION is set to introduce a more inclusive and inspiring approach to fitness competition for women in the UAE.

title: Dubai Sports Council launches Dubai Open Volleyball Academies Championship next Saturday
content:
DUBAI: The Dubai Sports Council announced the organisation of the ‘Dubai Open Volleyball Academies Championship’, the first of its kind in the region, that is scheduled to kick off on April 25 (Saturday), with the participation of 70 teams representing 25 academies and clubs from across the UAE. The championship is being held in cooperation with UAE Volleyball federation and Sports Mania and will continue until June 13, 2026.
The championship includes five age categories for males and females (under 10, 12, 14, 16, and 19 years old), and more than 250 matches are scheduled to be held at the Shabab Al Ahli Club indoor courts and the Al Safa Sports Hall in the Jumeirah area.
The Dubai Sports Council and the organising committee held a technical meeting with coaches and directors of participating academies. During the meeting, the technical and organisational regulations were reviewed, the match schedule was approved, and all participant inquiries were addressed.

Ali Omar Al Baloushi, Director of Sports Development at the Dubai Sports Council, emphasized that the Council prioritises talent discovery and development, stating: “We are working to build an integrated system to attract and nurture promising players across various sports. Launching this tournament reflects our commitment to providing a truly competitive environment that gives young athletes the opportunity to demonstrate their abilities and refine their skills by increasing the number of matches according to international standards.”
Al Baloushi added: “This tournament is part of the Council’s strategy to develop talent within Dubai clubs and enhance cooperation with the private sector to become an active partner in developing the sports sector by organising events that have a direct impact on youth development programmes.”

He also explained that the tournament complements a comprehensive strategic programme and joins the Dubai Open series of tournaments in football, basketball, handball, tennis, gymnastics, badminton and padel.
Tariq Abboud, Managing Director of Sports Mania, hailed the collaboration with the Dubai Sports Council, saying: “We are honoured to organise this tournament, which brings together government and private academies and clubs from across the country to compete in official matches that enhance the development of emerging talent.”
Abboud praised the high turnout and the keenness of coaches and team managers to attend the technical meeting, reflecting their strong enthusiasm for participating.
The participating clubs include Al Wasl, Shabab Al Ahli, Al Nasr, Hatta, and Al Dhaid, along with the academies of Wildcats, UIG Sports, FDR, Centrix, Centrline, One Dela Cruz, Next Gen, Hec Volleyball, Speed Sports, Spikers Abu Dhabi, Al Mawakeb, Abu Dhabi Volleyball Clinic, ATPV Com, Olympic Stars, and Esperia.

title: TCL brings Olympic-level performance home with next-generation QD-Mini LED TVs
content:
As the Winter Olympics once again showcased the speed, precision and intensity of elite sport, TCL used the global moment to reinforce a simple message for viewers at home: performance should not stop at the arena.
As a Worldwide Olympic Partner, the brand has been aligning itself with the values of excellence and innovation that define the Games. More importantly for consumers, that partnership is reflected in the technology TCL is putting into living rooms across the UAE.
At the centre of TCL’s offering is its QD-Mini LED TV lineup, a category where the company holds the position of Global No.1 Mini LED TV Brand, Global No.1 Ultra-Large Screen TV Brand and Global No.1 Google TV Brand, according to 2024 Omdia shipment data. For sports fans, those credentials translate into tangible viewing advantages rather than marketing claims.
Winter sports are among the most demanding types of content for any television. Bright white snow, rapid camera pans, high-speed motion and fine details all test a screen’s ability to handle contrast, clarity and brightness simultaneously.

TCL’s QD-Mini LED technology addresses this through ultra-precise backlight control, allowing the screen to manage light with far greater accuracy. The result is deeper blacks, brighter highlights and more defined details, even during fast transitions.
The flagship 115-inch X955 represents the most immersive expression of that technology. Designed as a stadium-scale display for the home, it combines exceptional brightness with refined contrast and expansive screen real estate.
When watching downhill skiing, figure skating or ice hockey, the scale alone transforms the experience, making viewers feel closer to the action. Subtle movements, such as the spray of ice during a sharp turn or the tracking of a puck across the rink, become clearer and more impactful.
For consumers who want high-performance sports viewing in slightly smaller formats, TCL’s 98-inch and 85-inch X11K models deliver strong brightness levels and advanced motion clarity that are particularly suited to fast-paced content. The 75-inch and 65-inch C8K series offer premium QD-Mini LED performance in more versatile sizes, balancing vivid color reproduction with smooth motion handling.
Across the lineup, the emphasis remains consistent: sharper detail, controlled light precision and immersive scale.

Motion clarity is especially critical when following live sport. Blurring during quick pans or high-speed sequences can reduce the sense of realism. TCL’s processing and backlight precision work together to maintain stability and smoothness, ensuring that split-second moments remain crisp.
For viewers in the UAE who regularly gather for major tournaments and international competitions, this level of clarity enhances not just individual enjoyment but shared viewing experiences as well.
While the display technology is the primary focus for sports fans, TCL’s broader home ecosystem also addresses another key regional consideration: climate. In a country where high temperatures are part of daily life, comfort is essential to any entertainment setup.
TCL’s VoxIN JetMax and SaveIN AI Invertor air-conditioning systems are engineered for fast cooling, intelligent temperature adaptation and energy-efficient performance in high heat and humidity.
JetMax is designed to deliver rapid temperature adjustment when returning home from the outdoors, while SaveIN AI Invertor optimizes energy consumption and maintains air quality to ensure consistent comfort.
Together, TCL’s large-format QD-Mini LED TVs and intelligent cooling solutions reflect a performance-led approach that mirrors the spirit of the Olympic Games. The same principles that define elite winter athletes – precision, endurance and control – are applied to how images are displayed and how environments are cooled.

For consumers, this means sharper sports visuals, immersive large-screen viewing and reliable comfort during long match days.
TCL’s recent Winter Olympics activation at Dubai Ice Rink provided visitors with an opportunity to experience these technologies firsthand. However, the real impact extends beyond the event itself.
The focus remains on delivering high-performance viewing solutions that elevate how sport is experienced at home, long after the final medal has been awarded.
As global competitions continue to unite audiences, the demand for clearer motion, brighter displays and larger screens will only grow. With its QD-Mini LED leadership and climate-ready cooling solutions, TCL is positioning itself as a premium technology partner for sports fans in the UAE who want every moment of the action to feel sharper, larger and closer to reality.
